title: The True Petitions of the Universal Pure True Path

intro.title: Introduction: The True Petitions of the Universal Pure True Path
paras: Vallalar, Ramalinga Adigal (1823–1874), laid four petitions before God. This volume gathers all four, in the order of the printed editions.

The Small True Petition recalls the many births we passed through and the compassion that brought us to this human body, and asks for the adornment of the Hall of Wisdom, for deathless life, and for the right of oneness in soul-kinship, the main aim of Suddha Sanmarkkam, the Pure True Path.

The Great True Petition tells what God's grace has done for him: from the darkness of ignorance before any body, through the father's seed and the mother's womb, to birth, childhood and youth. Grace made him know that there is only one true God, Arut Perum Jothi, the Supreme Light of Grace. It gave him the good endeavour of compassion that longs for all living beings to attain bliss.
The True Petition of Wisdom longs to know, contemplate and praise the holy presence of Grace, which even the true sages cannot tell as it is, and ends in knowing without knowing.

The True Petition of the Sangam asks to be freed in this very body from death, disease, old age, fear and suffering. Grace alone can give it, so Vallalar gives up every claim over body, experience and life, and asks the same eternal life for all living beings.

One thing is common among all four: Arut Perum Jothi, the Boundless Grace Light, real and open to every soul, whose grace gives Jeevakarunyam, compassion for all Life, the foundation of any real spirituality.
Each petition is given in Tamil, checked against the printed editions, with transliteration, translation and commentary.

intro.title: Introduction: The Small True Petition of the Pure True Path
paras: Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Siru Vinnappam (The Small True Petition) is a prose prayer of Ramalinga Adigal (Vallalar). Where the other three petitions say “I”, this one says “we”: it is a prayer for all who walk the path.

It opens by naming God: Natural Truth, Natural Intelligence, Natural Bliss, Arut Perum Jothi (the Supreme Light of Grace), the God of Great Compassion. Even the Vedas and Agamas find no words worthy of Him, so the petitioners ask Him to accept their small words.

Then they remember the soul’s long journey: born again and again as plants and stones, worms and fish, birds, animals, gods and demons, dying each time in pain. In pity, God placed them in this human body, which can reach the deathless great life.

Grace made them know that there is one true God, and that a Hall of Wisdom must be established at Vadalur as the sign of His dance of grace. As they adorn it, they pray that every human being become a true devotee and live for ever.

It ends with its heart: that religions, sects, caste and the stages of life, the chief obstacle to Suddha Sanmarkkam, never take hold of our minds, and that its chief aim, Anma Neya Orumaipadu Urimai, the right of oneness in soul-kinship, shine among us always.

intro.title: Introduction: The Great True Petition of the Universal Pure True Path
paras: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Peru Vinnappam (The Great True Petition) is a foundational prose work of Ramalinga Adigal (Vallalar).
Vallalar narrates how God cares for him more than any parent could, constantly protecting, nourishing and guiding him through every moment in the womb and through birth.
What is extraordinary is the detail with which he describes his life inside his mother's womb. He explains that the womb is dark, small and filled with dangers.

Thanks to the grace of Arut Perum Jothi (the Vast Grace Light), Ramalinga was born safely and passed through every danger of infancy and youth, becoming a man of perfect devotion and boundless compassion towards all living beings.

As he grew, grace showed him that caste customs are false, and that the religions, their gods and their holy books do not reach the truth. It showed him one God, Arut Perum Jothi, shining in every being, and one way to live: compassion for all life, Jeevakarunyam.

intro.title: Introduction: The True Petition of Wisdom of the Universal Pure True Path
paras: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Gnana Vinnappam (The True Petition of Wisdom) is a prose work of Ramalinga Adigal (Vallalar). The supplication is based around one main question: how can anyone know, contemplate and praise the holy presence of God’s grace?

The Vedas and Agamas measured it for ages and found no end. The lords of the universe dare not contemplate it; the gods dare not praise it. How then can Vallalar, calling himself a small one, know Him?
Yet, thanks to his longing for divine grace from the Arut Perum Jothi (the Boundless Light of Grace), he finally begins to realize Him.

The realized ones tell of the greatest sages. Asked to describe the holy presence of Grace as it is, some melt and sigh: “How shall we know it!” Others say no word at all; tears of bliss pour from their eyes, and they remain still.
God fills every stage of wisdom and, beyond them all, shines alone. So the petition ends in knowing without knowing, contemplating without contemplating, praising without praising.

intro.title: Introduction: The True Petition of the Sangam of the Universal Pure True Path
paras: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sanga Sathya Vinnappam (The True Petition of the Sangam) is the shortest of the four petitions of Ramalinga Adigal (Vallalar). He speaks it at Vadalur, before Arut Perum Jothi, who dances in the Hall of Wisdom so that every living being may have bliss.

It says plainly what he wants above all: to be freed in this very body from death, disease, old age, fear and suffering, and to make this body an eternal body, living for ever in the great life of bliss.

Grace made him know that nothing can give this except the freedom of God’s grace, and that this grace comes only when the three freedoms we claim as our own, over the body, over experience and over life, are given up.
So he gives all three to grace. The body, the life and everything we enjoy were given by God’s great compassion, not won by our own freedom.
Then he asks the same for every living being: that God make them know what He made him know, and make them heirs of that life. It ends with praise to the reign of God’s great compassion.

works.title: The Small True Petition of the Pure True Path

sections.title: The Small True Petition of Suddha Sanmarkkam

tamil: திருச்சிற்றம்பலம்
1. சுத்த சன்மார்க்க சத்தியச் சிறு விண்ணப்பம்
translit: tirucciṟṟampalam
1. cutta caṉmārkka cattiyac ciṟu viṇṇappam
translation: Tiruchitrambalam. The Small True Petition of Suddha Sanmarkkam.
commentary: Above the title stands the sacred word Tiruchitrambalam, as in Vallalar's own manuscript; the petition also closes with it. The word means "the holy small hall", the name of the hall of the sacred dance at Chidambaram. The title names the work a viṇṇappam, a petition laid before God, and calls it true (cattiya) and small (ciṟu). The petition explains the word small: those who pray call themselves smaller even than a straw, and their petitions small, made with small knowledge. It speaks as "we" (yāṅkaḷ) throughout, while its companion, the Great True Petition (Peru Vinnappam), speaks as "I". In the collected prose writings it stands first of the four petitions. The petitioners recall how they lay in the darkness of ignorance, passed through birth after birth, and were placed by God's compassion in a human body. As they begin to adorn the Hall of Wisdom, they ask God to make them, and the others in this world who have received this body, true devotees established in Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam. They name religions, sects and paths as the chief obstacle to Suddha Sanmarkkam, and ask that the customs, notions and distinctions of these, and the worldly customs, notions and distinctions such as varna (caste) and ashrama (the stages of life), never take hold of their minds. They ask that the chief aim of Suddha Sanmarkkam, Anma Neya Orumaipadu Urimai, the right of oneness in soul-kinship, fill and shine among them always.

sections.title: Invocation to the God of Great Compassion

tamil: இயற்கை உண்மையரென்றும், இயற்கை அறிவினரென்றும், இயற்கை இன்பினரென்றும், நிர்க்குணரென்றும், சிற்குணரென்றும், நித்தியரென்றும், சத்தியரென்றும், ஏகரென்றும், அநேகரென்றும், ஆதியரென்றும், அனாதியரென்றும், அமலரென்றும், அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதியரென்றும், அற்புதரென்றும், நிரதிசயரென்றும், எல்லாமானவரென்றும், எல்லாமுடையவரென்றும், எல்லாம் வல்லவரென்றும், குறிக்கப்படுதல் முதலிய அளவு கடந்த திருக்குறிப்புத் திருவார்த்தைகளாற் சுத்த சன்மார்க்க ஞானிகள் துதித்தும், நினைத்தும், உணர்ந்தும், புணர்ந்தும், அனுபவிக்க விளங்குகின்ற தனித்தலைமைப் பெரும் பதியாகிய பெருங்கருணைக் கடவுளே! தேவரீர் திருவருட் சமுகத்தில் துரும்பினும் சிறியேமாகிய யாங்கள் சிற்றறிவாற் செய்து கொள்ளும் சிறு விண்ணப்பங்களைத் திருச்செவிக்கேற்பித்தருளி யெங்களை இரக்ஷித்தருளல் வேண்டும்.
translit: iyaṟkai uṇmaiyareṉṟum, iyaṟkai aṟiviṉareṉṟum, iyaṟkai iṉpiṉareṉṟum, nirkkuṇareṉṟum, ciṟkuṇareṉṟum, nittiyareṉṟum, cattiyareṉṟum, ēkareṉṟum, anēkareṉṟum, ātiyareṉṟum, aṉātiyareṉṟum, amalareṉṟum, aruṭperuñjōtiyareṉṟum, aṟputareṉṟum, niraticayareṉṟum, ellāmāṉavareṉṟum, ellāmuṭaiyavareṉṟum, ellām vallavareṉṟum, kuṟikkappaṭutal mutaliya aḷavu kaṭanta tirukkuṟipput tiruvārttaikaḷāṟ cutta caṉmārkka ñāṉikaḷ tutittum, niṉaittum, uṇarntum, puṇarntum, aṉupavikka viḷaṅkukiṉṟa taṉittalaimaip perum patiyākiya peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭavuḷē! tēvarīr tiruvaruṭ camukattil turumpiṉum ciṟiyēmākiya yāṅkaḷ ciṟṟaṟivāṟ ceytu koḷḷum ciṟu viṇṇappaṅkaḷait tiruccevikkēṟpittaruḷi yeṅkaḷai irakṣittaruḷal vēṇṭum.
translation: You are named Natural Truth, Natural Intelligence and Natural Bliss; the One beyond the three qualities of nature and the One whose quality is Consciousness; the Eternal and the True; the One and the Many; the First, the One without beginning, and the Stainless; Arut Perum Jothi, the Supreme Light of Grace; the Wondrous and the Unsurpassed; the One who is all, the One who possesses all, and the One who can do all. You shine forth so that, through these and other sacred indications and sacred words beyond all measure, the sages of Suddha Sanmarkkam may praise You, think of You, realize You, unite with You, and so experience You. O God of Great Compassion, the Great Lord of unique supremacy! In the holy presence of Your grace, we, who are smaller even than a straw, make small petitions with our small knowledge. We pray that You graciously admit them to Your holy ear and protect us.
commentary: In the Tamil, this whole opening is one sentence. Name follows name, and all of them lead to a single cry: "O God of Great Compassion!" Before Vallalar asks for anything, he says to whom he is speaking.

The first three names are Truth, Intelligence and Bliss, each called natural (iyaṟkai): they are God's own nature, not made and not received from anything else. Several names come in pairs that seem to be opposites: beyond the three qualities of nature, yet with Consciousness as His quality; the One and the Many; the First and the One without beginning. Both sides of each pair are true of the one God. Among them stands Arut Perum Jothi, the Supreme Light of Grace, the name by which this petition calls on God again and again.

These names are sacred indications and sacred words, beyond measure; those given here are only some of them. Through them the sages of Suddha Sanmarkkam praise God, think of Him, realize Him and unite with Him. God is not out of reach: He shines forth so that they may experience Him. The last word before kaṭavuḷē, "O God", is great compassion (peruṅkaruṇai). It is to the God of Great Compassion that this petition is brought.

Then comes the first request, made as "we" (yāṅkaḷ). Smaller even than a straw, they make small petitions (ciṟu viṇṇappaṅkaḷ) with small knowledge (ciṟṟaṟivu), and they ask God to admit these to His holy ear and to protect them.

sections.title: Beyond the Words of the Vedas and Agamas

tamil: எல்லாச் சத்திகளும், எல்லாச் சத்தர்களும், எல்லாத் தலைவர்களும் அறிந்து கொள்ளுதற்கு மிகவு மரியதாய், எல்லாத் தத்துவங்களுக்கும், எல்லாத் தத்துவிகளுக்கும் அப்பால் அப்பாலாய் விளங்கும் ஓர் சுத்த ஞான வெளியில் தமக்கு ஒரு விதத்தாலும் ஒப்புயர்வு சிறிதுங் குறிக்கப்படாத தனிப்பெருந் தலைமை அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதியராகி விளங்குகின்ற தேவரீரது தனிப்பெருந் தன்மைக்கு மெய்யறிவுடையோரால் விதிக்கப்பட்ட வேதாகமங்களும் பெருந்தகை வாசகத்தைப் பெறாது சிறுதகை வாசகங்களைப் பெற்றுத் திகைப்படைகின்றன என்றால், மலத்திற் புழுத்த புழுவினுஞ் சிறியேமாகிய யாங்கள் திருச்சமுகத்தில் விண்ணப்பித்தற் குரிய பெருந்தகை வாசகத்தை எவ்வாறறிவோம்! எங்ஙனஞ் செய்வோம்! ஆகலில், கருணாநிதியாகிய கடவுளே! யாங்கள் விண்ணப்பிக்கின்ற அற்ப வாசகத்தில் உரிமை நோக்காது அங்கீகரித்தருளி யெங்களைக் காத்தருளல் வேண்டும்.
translit: ellāc cattikaḷum, ellāc cattarkaḷum, ellāt talaivarkaḷum aṟintu koḷḷutaṟku mikavu mariyatāy, ellāt tattuvaṅkaḷukkum, ellāt tattuvikaḷukkum appāl appālāy viḷaṅkum ōr cutta ñāṉa veḷiyil tamakku oru vitattālum oppuyarvu ciṟituṅ kuṟikkappaṭāta taṉipperun talaimai aruṭperuñjōtiyarāki viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tēvarīratu taṉipperun taṉmaikku meyyaṟivuṭaiyōrāl vitikkappaṭṭa vētākamaṅkaḷum peruntakai vācakattaip peṟātu ciṟutakai vācakaṅkaḷaip peṟṟut tikaippaṭaikiṉṟaṉa eṉṟāl, malattiṟ puḻutta puḻuviṉuñ ciṟiyēmākiya yāṅkaḷ tiruccamukattil viṇṇappittaṟ kuriya peruntakai vācakattai evvāṟaṟivōm! eṅṅaṉañ ceyvōm! ākalil, karuṇānitiyākiya kaṭavuḷē! yāṅkaḷ viṇṇappikkiṉṟa aṟpa vācakattil urimai nōkkātu aṅkīkarittaruḷi yeṅkaḷaik kāttaruḷal vēṇṭum.
translation: There is a Pure Space of Wisdom that all the energies, all their agents and all the lords find exceedingly hard to know, and that shines far, far beyond all the tattvas and all the tattvis, the beings who preside over them. In that Space You shine as Arut Perum Jothi, unique and supreme; in no way at all can any equal or any superior to You be pointed to. For this unique greatness of Yours, even the Vedas and Agamas laid down by those of true knowledge find no words of great worth. They find only words of small worth, and they stand bewildered. If that is so, how shall we, who are smaller even than the worm bred in dung, know words of great worth fit to petition in Your holy presence! How shall we make them! Therefore, O God, Treasure of Compassion! Do not weigh whether the petty words of our petition are fitting. Graciously accept them and protect us.
commentary: Vallalar first says where God shines. Far, far beyond all the tattvas, the constituents of body, mind and world, and beyond all the beings who preside over them, lies a Pure Space of Wisdom (cutta ñāṉa veḷi). All the energies, their agents and all the lords find that Space exceedingly hard to know. In it God shines as Arut Perum Jothi, with no equal and none above. Vallalar then says plainly that the Vedas and Agamas, laid down by people of true knowledge, find only "words of small worth" (ciṟutakai vācakam) for this greatness, and stand bewildered. If even they fail, how could "we", smaller even than a worm bred in dung, find fitting words? So the petitioners ask God, the Treasure of Compassion, to accept their poor words without weighing whether they are fitting, and to protect them.

sections.title: Dwelling in Ignorance

tamil: தாயினுஞ் சிறந்த தயவுடைக் கடவுளே! இயற்கையே அஞ்ஞான விருளில் அஞ்ஞான வுருவில் அஞ்ஞானிகளாய் அஞ்ஞானத்திற் பயின்று ஏதுந் தெரியாது கிடந்த எங்களைத் தேவரீர் பெருங்கருணையாற் பவுதிக வுடம்பிற் சிறிதறிவு தோற்றி விடுத்த அஞ்ஞான்று தொட்டு இஞ்ஞான்று வரையும், அது கொண்டு அறிவே வடிவாய், அறிவே யுருவாய், அறிவே பொறியாய், அறிவே மனமாய், அறிவே யறிவாய், அறிவே யனுபவமாய் அனுபவிக்கத் தெரிந்து கொள்ளாது, குற்றமே வடிவாய்க், குற்றமே யுருவாய்க், குற்றமே பொறியாய்க், குற்றமே மனமாய்க், குற்றமே யறிவாய்க், குற்றமே யனுபவமாய் அனுபவிக்கின்ற சிறியேங்கள் திருச்சமுகத்தில் விண்ணப்பிக்கின்ற விண்ணப்பமும் குற்றமே வடிவாய்க் குற்றமே குறிக்குமென் றறிந்தோமாயினும், குற்றங்குறியாத வகை விண்ணப்பஞ் செய்தற்கு ஒருவாற்றானு முணர்ச்சி யில்லோ மாதலிற் றுணிவு கொண்டு விண்ணப்பிக்கின்றோம். குற்றங்களையே குணங்களாகக் கொள்ளுதல் தேவரீர் திருவருட் பெருமைக்கியற்கையாதலின் இவ்விண்ணப்பங்களிற் குற்றங்குறியாது கடைக்கணித்தருளிக் கருணை செய்தல் வேண்டும்.
translit: tāyiṉuñ ciṟanta tayavuṭaik kaṭavuḷē! iyaṟkaiyē aññāṉa viruḷil aññāṉa vuruvil aññāṉikaḷāy aññāṉattiṟ payiṉṟu ētun teriyātu kiṭanta eṅkaḷait tēvarīr peruṅkaruṇaiyāṟ pavutika vuṭampiṟ ciṟitaṟivu tōṟṟi viṭutta aññāṉṟu toṭṭu iññāṉṟu varaiyum, atu koṇṭu aṟivē vaṭivāy, aṟivē yuruvāy, aṟivē poṟiyāy, aṟivē maṉamāy, aṟivē yaṟivāy, aṟivē yaṉupavamāy aṉupavikkat terintu koḷḷātu, kuṟṟamē vaṭivāyk, kuṟṟamē yuruvāyk, kuṟṟamē poṟiyāyk, kuṟṟamē maṉamāyk, kuṟṟamē yaṟivāyk, kuṟṟamē yaṉupavamāy aṉupavikkiṉṟa ciṟiyēṅkaḷ tiruccamukattil viṇṇappikkiṉṟa viṇṇappamum kuṟṟamē vaṭivāyk kuṟṟamē kuṟikkumeṉ ṟaṟintōmāyiṉum, kuṟṟaṅkuṟiyāta vakai viṇṇappañ ceytaṟku oruvāṟṟāṉu muṇarcci yillō mātaliṟ ṟuṇivu koṇṭu viṇṇappikkiṉṟōm. kuṟṟaṅkaḷaiyē kuṇaṅkaḷākak koḷḷutal tēvarīr tiruvaruṭ perumaikkiyaṟkaiyātaliṉ ivviṇṇappaṅkaḷiṟ kuṟṟaṅkuṟiyātu kaṭaikkaṇittaruḷik karuṇai ceytal vēṇṭum.
translation: O God whose compassion surpasses even a mother's! By our very nature we lay in the darkness of ignorance, in the form of ignorance, as ignorant beings dwelling in ignorance, knowing nothing at all. In Your great compassion You made a little knowledge arise in us in a physical body and sent us forth. From that day to this, we have not learned to use that knowledge to experience with knowledge alone as our form, knowledge alone as our shape, knowledge alone as our senses, knowledge alone as our mind, knowledge alone as our knowing, and knowledge alone as our experience. Instead, we small ones experience with nothing but fault as our form, fault as our shape, fault as our senses, fault as our mind, fault as our knowing, and fault as our experience. We know that even the petition we make in Your holy presence is nothing but fault in its form and points to nothing but fault. Yet we have no understanding at all of how to petition without fault, so we take courage and petition. To take even faults as virtues is natural to the greatness of Your grace. So do not mark the faults in these petitions. Cast Your gracious glance upon us and show us compassion.
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as more compassionate than a mother. The petitioners confess where they began. By nature they lay in the darkness of ignorance (aññāṉam), dwelling in ignorance and knowing nothing; the Tamil words in the heading are taken from this line. Like the Tamil captions of sections 5 to 15, they are not Vallalar's own: the printed editions do not have them. That was their state before any of the births they go on to tell. By His great compassion God made a little knowledge arise in them in a physical body; the Great True Petition gives the same testimony. They did not learn to use that knowledge so that knowledge alone became their form, senses, mind and experience. Instead, they say, fault alone has become all of these, and even this petition is nothing but fault. They do not know how to petition without fault, and so they take courage and petition as they are. Their hope rests on this: it is natural to the greatness of God's grace to take even faults as virtues. So they ask Him not to mark their faults, and to look on them with compassion.

sections.title: Stationary Births

tamil: அஞ்ஞான விருளில் ஒன்றுந் தெரியா துணர்ச்சி யின்றிக்கிடந்த காலம் போக, அவ்விருளை விட்டு நீங்கிய காலத்தே, இவ்வுலகினிடத்து புல், நெல், மரம், செடி, பூடு முதலியவாகவும் கல், மலை, குன்று முதலியவாகவும் பிறந்து பிறந்து, களையுண்டல், வெட்டுண்டல், அறுப்புண்டல், கிள்ளுண்டல், உலர்ப்புண்டல், உடைப்புண்டல், வெடிப்புண்டல் முதலிய பலவேறு அவத்தைகளால் இறந்து இறந்து அத்தாவரயோனி வர்க்கங்களெல்லாஞ் சென்று சென்று, உழன்று உழன்று அலுப்படைந்தேம்;
translit: aññāṉa viruḷil oṉṟun teriyā tuṇarcci yiṉṟikkiṭanta kālam pōka, avviruḷai viṭṭu nīṅkiya kālattē, ivvulakiṉiṭattu pul, nel, maram, ceṭi, pūṭu mutaliyavākavum kal, malai, kuṉṟu mutaliyavākavum piṟantu piṟantu, kaḷaiyuṇṭal, veṭṭuṇṭal, aṟuppuṇṭal, kiḷḷuṇṭal, ularppuṇṭal, uṭaippuṇṭal, veṭippuṇṭal mutaliya palavēṟu avattaikaḷāl iṟantu iṟantu attāvarayōṉi varkkaṅkaḷellāñ ceṉṟu ceṉṟu, uḻaṉṟu uḻaṉṟu aluppaṭaintēm;
translation: When the time we lay in the darkness of ignorance, knowing nothing and feeling nothing, had passed, and we came out of that darkness, we were born again and again in this world as grass, paddy, trees, bushes, herbs, and the like, and as stones, mountains, hills, and the like. We died again and again through various afflictions such as being weeded out, chopped down, reaped, plucked, dried out, shattered, and blasted. Passing continuously through all those categories of stationary birth, wandering endlessly, we became thoroughly exhausted.
commentary: Vallalar now tells God the story of our births. First came the time in the darkness of ignorance, when we knew nothing and felt nothing. When that time passed and we came out of the darkness, our first births were among things fixed in one place (tāvaram, stationary): grass, paddy, trees, bushes, and herbs, and also stones, mountains, and hills. Bound to one spot, we were weeded out, chopped down, reaped, plucked, dried out, shattered, and blasted, and we died again and again until we were completely worn out. Vallalar counts even stones and hills among the births we passed through.

sections.title: Crawling and Water-dwelling Births

tamil: பின்னர் எறும்பு, செல், புழு, பாம்பு, உடும்பு, பல்லி முதலியவாகவும் தவளை, சிறுமீன், முதலை, சுறா, திமிங்கிலம் முதலியவாகவும் பிறந்து பிறந்து, தேய்ப்புண்டல், நசுக்குண்டல், அடியுண்டல், பிடியுண்டல் முதலிய பல வேறு அவத்தைகளால் இறந்து இறந்து அவ்வூர்வன நீர் வாழ்வன யோனிவர்க்கங்க ளெல்லாஞ் சென்று சென்று, உழன்று உழன்று அலுப்படைந்தேம்;
translit: piṉṉar eṟumpu, cel, puḻu, pāmpu, uṭumpu, palli mutaliyavākavum tavaḷai, ciṟumīṉ, mutalai, cuṟā, timiṅkilam mutaliyavākavum piṟantu piṟantu, tēyppuṇṭal, nacukkuṇṭal, aṭiyuṇṭal, piṭiyuṇṭal mutaliya pala vēṟu avattaikaḷāl iṟantu iṟantu avvūrvaṉa nīr vāḻvaṉa yōṉivarkkaṅka ḷellāñ ceṉṟu ceṉṟu, uḻaṉṟu uḻaṉṟu aluppaṭaintēm;
translation: Later, we were born again and again as ants, termites, worms, snakes, monitor lizards, wall lizards, and the like, and as frogs, small fish, crocodiles, sharks, whales, and the like. We died again and again through various afflictions such as being scraped away, crushed, beaten, and caught. Passing continuously through all those categories of crawling and water-dwelling birth, wandering endlessly, we became thoroughly exhausted.
commentary: Vallalar tells God that we were next born among the creatures that crawl and the creatures that live in water. He names them: ants, termites, worms, snakes, and lizards; frogs, small fish, crocodiles, sharks, and whales. In these bodies we were scraped away, crushed, beaten, and caught, and we died again and again. Then he repeats his refrain to God: we passed through all these crawling and water-dwelling births, wandering endlessly, until we were thoroughly exhausted. Vallalar counts himself among them. It was we, he says, who lived these lives and died these deaths.

sections.title: Winged Births

tamil: பின்னர் ஈ, வண்டு, தும்பி, குருவி, காக்கை, பருந்து, கழுகு முதலியவாகப் பிறந்து பிறந்து, அடியுண்டல், பிடியுண்டல், அலைப்புண்டல், உலைப்புண்டல் முதலிய பலவேறு அவத்தைகளால் இறந்திறந்து அப்பறவையோனி வர்க்கங் களெல்லாஞ் சென்று சென்று உழன் றுழன்று அலுப்படைந்தேம்;
translit: piṉṉar ī, vaṇṭu, tumpi, kuruvi, kākkai, paruntu, kaḻuku mutaliyavākap piṟantu piṟantu, aṭiyuṇṭal, piṭiyuṇṭal, alaippuṇṭal, ulaippuṇṭal mutaliya palavēṟu avattaikaḷāl iṟantiṟantu appaṟavaiyōṉi varkkaṅ kaḷellāñ ceṉṟu ceṉṟu uḻaṉ ṟuḻaṉṟu aluppaṭaintēm;
translation: Later, we were born again and again as flies, beetles, bees, sparrows, crows, kites, eagles, and the like. We died again and again through various afflictions such as being beaten, caught, tossed about, and tormented. Passing continuously through all those categories of winged birth, wandering endlessly, we became thoroughly exhausted.
commentary: Vallalar tells God that we were next born among the winged creatures, from flies and bees to crows and eagles. In his refrain he calls these the bird births (paṟavaiyōṉi), yet he places flies, beetles, and bees in that class with the sparrows and kites: it is the class of winged creatures. In these bodies we were beaten, caught, tossed about, and tormented, and we died again and again. Then the refrain returns unchanged: we passed through all these winged births until we were thoroughly exhausted. The fly that is swatted and the bird that is caught are living what Vallalar says we ourselves once lived.

sections.title: Animal Births

tamil: பின்னர் அணில், குரங்கு, நாய், பன்றி, பூனை, ஆடு, மாடு, யானை, குதிரை, புலி, கரடி முதலியவாகப் பிறந்து பிறந்து பிடியுண்டல், அடியுண்டல், குத்துண்டல், வெட்டுண்டல், தாக்குண்டல், கட்டுண்டல், தட்டுண்டல் முதலிய பல்வேறு அவத்தைகளால் இறந்திறந்து அவ்விலங்குயோனி வர்க்கங்க ளெல்லாஞ் சென்று சென்று, உழன்றுழன்று அலுப்படைந்தேம்;
translit: piṉṉar aṇil, kuraṅku, nāy, paṉṟi, pūṉai, āṭu, māṭu, yāṉai, kutirai, puli, karaṭi mutaliyavākap piṟantu piṟantu piṭiyuṇṭal, aṭiyuṇṭal, kuttuṇṭal, veṭṭuṇṭal, tākkuṇṭal, kaṭṭuṇṭal, taṭṭuṇṭal mutaliya palvēṟu avattaikaḷāl iṟantiṟantu avvilaṅkuyōṉi varkkaṅka ḷellāñ ceṉṟu ceṉṟu, uḻaṉṟuḻaṉṟu aluppaṭaintēm;
translation: Later, we were born again and again as squirrels, monkeys, dogs, pigs, cats, goats, cattle, elephants, horses, tigers, bears, and the like. We died again and again through various afflictions such as being caught, beaten, stabbed, slashed, attacked, tied up, and struck. Passing continuously through all those categories of animal birth, wandering endlessly, we became thoroughly exhausted.
commentary: Vallalar tells God that we were then born as animals, from squirrels and dogs to elephants, tigers, and bears. He names what was done to us in those bodies: we were caught, beaten, stabbed, slashed, attacked, tied up, and struck, and we died again and again until we were thoroughly exhausted. The animal that is caught, tied, or beaten today is a soul on the road we ourselves have walked. Here the ground of Jeevakarunyam, compassion for all living beings, stands plain: it is the foundation of the spiritual life Vallalar teaches.

sections.title: Deva Births

tamil: பின்னர் பசாசர், பூதர், இராக்கதர், அசுரர், சுரர் முதலியராகப் பிறந்து பிறந்து, அலைப்படுதல், அகப்படுதல், அகங்கரித்தல், அதிகரித்தல், மறந்து நிற்றல், நினைந்து நிற்றல், மயக்குறுதல், திகைப்புறுதல், போரிடுதல், கொலைபடுதல் முதலிய பல்வேறு அவத்தைகளால் இறந்து இறந்து அத்தேவயோனி வர்க்கங்க ளெல்லாஞ் சென்று சென்று, உழன் றுழன்று அலுப்படைந்தேம்;
translit: piṉṉar pacācar, pūtar, irākkatar, acurar, curar mutaliyarākap piṟantu piṟantu, alaippaṭutal, akappaṭutal, akaṅkarittal, atikarittal, maṟantu niṟṟal, niṉaintu niṟṟal, mayakkuṟutal, tikaippuṟutal, pōriṭutal, kolaipaṭutal mutaliya palvēṟu avattaikaḷāl iṟantu iṟantu attēvayōṉi varkkaṅka ḷellāñ ceṉṟu ceṉṟu, uḻaṉ ṟuḻaṉṟu aluppaṭaintēm;
translation: Later, we were born again and again as ghouls, goblins, demons, titans, gods, and the like. We died again and again through various afflictions such as being tossed about, being trapped, acting with arrogance, exercising authority, remaining in forgetfulness, remaining lost in thought, becoming deluded, becoming bewildered, fighting, and being killed. Passing continuously through all those categories of deva birth, wandering endlessly, we became thoroughly exhausted.
commentary: Vallalar tells God that we were also born in the deva births (tēvayōṉi): as ghouls, goblins, demons, titans, and gods (curar). Here tēva names these beings; it does not mean God. The afflictions of these births are of another kind. We were tossed about and trapped; we grew arrogant and exercised authority; we stayed forgetful or lost in thought; we were deluded and bewildered; we fought and were killed. Even arrogance and authority are counted among the afflictions through which we died again and again. So we passed through all these births too, until we were thoroughly exhausted.

sections.title: Hellish Births

tamil: பின்னர் காட்டகத்தார், கரவு செய்வார், கொலை செய்வார் முதலியராகப் பிறந்து பிறந்து பயப்படல், சிறைப்படல், சிதைபடல் முதலிய அவத்தைகளால் இறந்திறந்து அந்நரகயோனி வர்க்கங்களெல்லாஞ் சென்று சென்று, உழன்றுழன்று அலுப்படைந்தேம்.
translit: piṉṉar kāṭṭakattār, karavu ceyvār, kolai ceyvār mutaliyarākap piṟantu piṟantu payappaṭal, ciṟaippaṭal, citaipaṭal mutaliya avattaikaḷāl iṟantiṟantu annarakayōṉi varkkaṅkaḷellāñ ceṉṟu ceṉṟu, uḻaṉṟuḻaṉṟu aluppaṭaintēm.
translation: Later, we were born again and again as dwellers in the wild, deceivers, killers, and the like. We died again and again through afflictions such as fear, imprisonment, and being broken apart. Passing continuously through all those categories of hellish birth, wandering endlessly, we became thoroughly exhausted.
commentary: Vallalar tells God that we were also born into the hellish births: as dwellers in the wild (kāṭṭakattār), as deceivers, and as killers. He says "we", and so counts himself among them. In those births we died again and again through fear, imprisonment, and being broken apart, until we were thoroughly exhausted. Killing (kolai) is named here among the marks of hellish birth. With this the long list of births ends. The next lines say what brought it to an end: God took our exhaustion into His heart and, in compassion, placed us in this human body.

sections.title: No Return We Can Make

tamil: அங்ஙனம் யாங்கள் அப்பிறவிகள் தோறும் அடைந்த அலுப்பும் அச்சமும் அவலமும் களைப்பும் துன்பமும், திருவுளத் தடைத்து இரங்கியருளி அழியாப் பெருவாழ்வைப் பெறுதற்குரிய உயரறிவுடைய இம்மனித தேகத்தில் செலுத்தியருளிய தேவரீரது பெருங்கருணைக்கு யாங்கள் செய்யுங் கைம்மாறு ஒன்றுந் தெரிந்தோமில்லை.
translit: aṅṅaṉam yāṅkaḷ appiṟavikaḷ tōṟum aṭainta aluppum accamum avalamum kaḷaippum tuṉpamum, tiruvuḷat taṭaittu iraṅkiyaruḷi aḻiyāp peruvāḻvaip peṟutaṟkuriya uyaraṟivuṭaiya immaṉita tēkattil celuttiyaruḷiya tēvarīratu peruṅkaruṇaikku yāṅkaḷ ceyyuṅ kaimmāṟu oṉṟun terintōmillai.
translation: You took into Your divine heart the exhaustion, fear, anguish, weariness, and sorrow that we went through in this way in each of those births. Taking pity on us, You graciously placed us in this human body, which has the high intelligence fit for attaining the imperishable great life. For this immense compassion of Yours, we know of no recompense at all that we could make.
commentary: Here the petition turns from the long list of births to God's compassion. In each of those births we went through exhaustion, fear, anguish, weariness, and sorrow. God took all of it into His own heart, took pity on us, and placed us in this human body. Vallalar says why this body matters: it has the high intelligence fit for attaining the imperishable great life (aḻiyāp peruvāḻvu), the life free of death. Before such compassion he confesses that we know of no recompense (kaimmāṟu) at all that we could make. The human body is God's gift, given out of compassion.

sections.title: Wasted Time

tamil: உயிர்களின் அகத்தும் புறத்தும் அகப்புறத்தும் புறப்புறத்தும் நீக்கமின்றி நிறைந்து விளங்குகின்ற அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி ஆண்டவரே! இம்மனித தேகத்திற் செலுத்திய காலத்திலும் தாய் வயிற்றிலும் சிசுப் பருவத்திலும் குமாரப் பருவத்திலும் பல வேறு அவத்தைகளால் அறிவின்றி யிருந்தோமாகலில், தேவரீர் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை அறிந்து கொள்ளாமல் வீண்போது கழித்தோம்.
translit: uyirkaḷiṉ akattum puṟattum akappuṟattum puṟappuṟattum nīkkamiṉṟi niṟaintu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa aruṭperuñjōti āṇṭavarē! immaṉita tēkattiṟ celuttiya kālattilum tāy vayiṟṟilum cicup paruvattilum kumārap paruvattilum pala vēṟu avattaikaḷāl aṟiviṉṟi yiruntōmākalil, tēvarīr peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai aṟintu koḷḷāmal vīṇpōtu kaḻittōm.
translation: O Lord Arut Perum Jothi, shining in all living beings and filling their inner, outer, inner-outer, and outer-outer without any gap! Even in the time You placed us in this human body, in the mother's womb, in infancy, and in boyhood, we were without knowledge because of many different afflictions. So we spent our time in vain, without coming to know the nature of Your immense compassion.
commentary: Vallalar calls on Arut Perum Jothi as the Lord who shines in every living being, filling its inner, outer, inner-outer, and outer-outer and leaving no gap. No living being stands outside this Light, and none is far from it. That Lord was never absent from us. Yet from the time God placed us in this human body, through the time in the womb, in infancy, and in boyhood, many different afflictions left us without knowledge, and we did not come to know His immense compassion. Vallalar calls that time wasted (vīṇpōtu) and names the loss plainly before God.

sections.title: One True God

tamil: அப்பருவங் கழிய இப்பருவத்தினிடத்தே, எல்லா அண்டங்களையும், எல்லா உலகங்களையும், எல்லா உயிர்களையும், எல்லாப் பொருள்களையும், மற்றை யெல்லாவற்றையும் தோற்றுவித்தும், விளக்கஞ் செய்வித்தும், துரிசு நீக்குவித்தும், பக்குவம் வருவித்தும், பலன் தருவித்தும், எங்கும் பூரணராகி விளங்குகின்ற ஓர் உண்மைக் கடவுள் உண்டென்றும், அக்கடவுளை உண்மையன்பாற் கருத்திற் கருதி வழிபாடு செய்யின் அக்கடவுள் திருவருள் நமது கருத்தின்கண் வெளிப்பட்டு விளங்குமென்றும், அத்திருவருள் விளக்கத்தால் மரணம், பிணி, மூப்பு, பயம், துன்பம் முதலிய அவத்தைகளெல்லாவற்றையும் தவிர்த்து எக்காலத்தும் எவ்விடத்தும் எவ்விதத்தும் எவ்வளவுந் தடைபடாத பேரின்ப சித்திப் பெருவாழ்வை யடைதல் கூடுமென்றும், எங்கள் அறிவில் தேவரீர் திருவருளால் உண்மைப்பட வுணர்த்தியருளப் பெற்றோம்.
translit: apparuvaṅ kaḻiya ipparuvattiṉiṭattē, ellā aṇṭaṅkaḷaiyum, ellā ulakaṅkaḷaiyum, ellā uyirkaḷaiyum, ellāp poruḷkaḷaiyum, maṟṟai yellāvaṟṟaiyum tōṟṟuvittum, viḷakkañ ceyvittum, turicu nīkkuvittum, pakkuvam varuvittum, palaṉ taruvittum, eṅkum pūraṇarāki viḷaṅkukiṉṟa ōr uṇmaik kaṭavuḷ uṇṭeṉṟum, akkaṭavuḷai uṇmaiyaṉpāṟ karuttiṟ karuti vaḻipāṭu ceyyiṉ akkaṭavuḷ tiruvaruḷ namatu karuttiṉkaṇ veḷippaṭṭu viḷaṅkumeṉṟum, attiruvaruḷ viḷakkattāl maraṇam, piṇi, mūppu, payam, tuṉpam mutaliya avattaikaḷellāvaṟṟaiyum tavirttu ekkālattum evviṭattum evvitattum evvaḷavun taṭaipaṭāta pēriṉpa cittip peruvāḻvai yaṭaital kūṭumeṉṟum, eṅkaḷ aṟivil tēvarīr tiruvaruḷāl uṇmaippaṭa vuṇarttiyaruḷap peṟṟōm.
translation: When that stage of life had passed, in this present stage You made us know truly, in our own understanding, by Your grace: There is one true God, who shines everywhere as the Complete One. He brings into being all universes, all worlds, all living beings, all things and everything else; He makes them shine, removes their impurity, brings them to ripeness and grants them their fruit. If we hold this God in our thought with true love and worship Him, His grace will appear and shine in our minds. By the illumination of that grace we can be freed from death, disease, old age, fear, suffering and all such afflictions, and attain the great life that is the attainment of supreme bliss, hindered at no time, in no place, in no way and to no degree.
commentary: Now that the years of childhood ignorance have passed, Vallalar tells God how His grace (aruḷ) has finally revealed the truth to them. By that grace they were made to know that there is one true God, who brings into being all universes, all worlds, all living beings and all things, makes them shine, removes their impurity, brings them to ripeness and grants them their fruit. When a person worships this single God with true love, that divine grace lights up their mind and conquers every human affliction, wiping out disease, old age, and even death itself to grant a perfect, endless life of bliss.

sections.title: When Shall We Worship?

tamil: அவ்வுணர்ச்சியைப் பெற்றது தொடங்கிக் கடவுள் வழிபாடு எஞ்ஞான்று செய்வோம்? கடவுள் திருவருள் விளக்கம் எந்நாளடைவோம்? மரணம், பிணி, மூப்பு, முதலிய அவத்தைகள் எப்போது நீங்கும்? என்று மழியாத பேரின்ப சித்தி எக்காலங் கிடைக்கும்? என்று எண்ணி யெண்ணி வழிதுறை தெரியாமல் வருந்தி நின்ற தருணத்தே—
translit: avvuṇarcciyaip peṟṟatu toṭaṅkik kaṭavuḷ vaḻipāṭu eññāṉṟu ceyvōm? kaṭavuḷ tiruvaruḷ viḷakkam ennāḷaṭaivōm? maraṇam, piṇi, mūppu, mutaliya avattaikaḷ eppōtu nīṅkum? eṉṟu maḻiyāta pēriṉpa citti ekkālaṅ kiṭaikkum? eṉṟu eṇṇi yeṇṇi vaḻituṟai teriyāmal varunti niṉṟa taruṇattē,
translation: From the time we received that understanding, we kept thinking: "When shall we worship God? On what day shall we attain the illumination of God's grace? When will death, disease, old age and the other afflictions leave us? When shall we receive the never-perishing attainment of supreme bliss?" Not knowing the way or the means, we stood grieving.
commentary: Grace had made the truth known to them: there is one true God, and if they worship Him with true love, His grace will shine in their minds and can bring them to the great life of supreme bliss. From then on they kept thinking about when all this would come to pass. Vallalar gives their four questions in their own words: When shall we worship God? On what day shall we attain the illumination of His grace? When will death, disease, old age and the other afflictions leave us? When shall we receive the attainment of supreme bliss that never perishes? They asked these again and again, but they did not know the way or the means (vaḻituṟai). So they stood in sorrow, longing for the day when old age, disease and death would give way to lasting bliss. In the Tamil the sentence does not end here. It was at that very time of grieving that God answered them, as the next section tells.

sections.title: A Hall of Wisdom to Be Established

tamil: களைப்பறிந்துதவுங் கருணைக் கடலாகிய கடவுளே! தேவரீர் "நெடுங்காலம் மரண முதலாகிய அவத்தைகளால் துன்பமுற்றுக் களைப்படைந்த உங்களை அவ்வவத்தைகளினின்றும் நீக்கிக் களைப்புங் கலக்கமுந் தவிர்த்து அழியாத பேரின்ப சித்தியை அடைவித்தற் பொருட்டாகவே பூர்வஞான சிதம்பரத்தின் வடபால் பார்வதிபுரமென்று குறிக்கப்படுகின்ற உத்தரஞான சித்திபுரத்தில் யாம் அளவுகடந்த நெடுங்காலம் சித்தியெல்லாம் விளங்கத் திருவருள் நடஞ்செய்வோ" மென்றும், "அது தருணம் மிகவும் அடுத்து சமீபித்த தருண" மென்றும், "அப்பதியினிடத்தே யாம் அருள் நடம் புரிதற்கு அடையாளமாக ஓர் ஞான சபை காணுதல் வேண்டு" மென்றும் திருவருட்குறிப்பால் அறிவித்தது மன்றி, அருளுருவாகி எங்களகத்தும் புறத்தும் அமர்ந்தருளி யாதோர் தடைகளுமின்றி அத்திருஞான சபையுந் தோன்றி விளங்கச் செய்வித்தருளிய தேவரீர் பெருங்கருணையைக் கருதுந்தோறும் பெருங்களிப்படைகின்றோம்.
translit: kaḷaippaṟintutavuṅ karuṇaik kaṭalākiya kaṭavuḷē! tēvarīr "neṭuṅkālam maraṇa mutalākiya avattaikaḷāl tuṉpamuṟṟuk kaḷaippaṭainta uṅkaḷai avvavattaikaḷiṉiṉṟum nīkkik kaḷaippuṅ kalakkamun tavirttu aḻiyāta pēriṉpa cittiyai aṭaivittaṟ poruṭṭākavē pūrvañāṉa citamparattiṉ vaṭapāl pārvatipurameṉṟu kuṟikkappaṭukiṉṟa uttarañāṉa cittipurattil yām aḷavukaṭanta neṭuṅkālam cittiyellām viḷaṅkat tiruvaruḷ naṭañceyvō" meṉṟum, "atu taruṇam mikavum aṭuttu camīpitta taruṇa" meṉṟum, "appatiyiṉiṭattē yām aruḷ naṭam puritaṟku aṭaiyāḷamāka ōr ñāṉa capai kāṇutal vēṇṭu" meṉṟum tiruvaruṭkuṟippāl aṟivittatu maṉṟi, aruḷuruvāki eṅkaḷakattum puṟattum amarntaruḷi yātōr taṭaikaḷumiṉṟi attiruñāṉa capaiyun tōṉṟi viḷaṅkac ceyvittaruḷiya tēvarīr peruṅkaruṇaiyaik karutuntōṟum peruṅkaḷippaṭaikiṉṟōm.
translation: O God, ocean of compassion, who knows our weariness and helps us! It was then that You made known to us, through the intimation of Your grace: "You have long suffered under death and the other afflictions, and you are weary. It is to free you from those afflictions, to end your weariness and distress, and to bring you to the imperishable attainment of supreme bliss, that We shall perform the dance of grace for an immeasurably long time, so that every siddhi shines forth, in Uttara Jnana Siddhipuram, which is called Parvatipuram, north of the ancient Jnana Chidambaram. That time is very near; it has come close. As a sign of Our performing the dance of grace in that place, a Hall of Wisdom must be established." Besides making this known, You took the form of grace and, graciously abiding within us and outside us, caused that holy Hall of Wisdom to arise and shine without any obstacle. Each time we think of this great compassion of Yours, we are filled with great joy.
commentary: Vallalar calls God the ocean of compassion who knows their weariness and helps. He recalls what God made known through the intimation of grace, and gives it in God's own words: that is why the Tamil says "you" (உங்களை) to the petitioners. To free them from death and the other afflictions and bring them to the imperishable attainment of supreme bliss, God will perform the dance of grace for an immeasurably long time in Uttara Jnana Siddhipuram, called Parvatipuram, north of Chidambaram; this is Vadalur. The time is near, and as a sign of that dance a Hall of Wisdom must be established. Then, abiding as grace within them and outside them, God made the Hall itself arise without any obstacle. It stands at Vadalur as the Sathya Jnana Sabha. Each time they remember this compassion, they are filled with great joy.

sections.title: The Adornment of the Hall

tamil: இனி அத்திருஞான சபையை அலங்கரித்தல் வேண்டுமெனக் குறிப்பித்த வண்ணம் அலங்கரிக்கத் தொடங்குகின்றோம்.

அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி யாண்டவரே! தேவரீர் அருளுருவாகி எங்கள் அகத்தும் புறத்தும் அமர்ந்தருளி யாங்கள் செய்யும் இவ்வலங்காரத்திருப்பணியில் எவ்விதத்தாலும் யாதொரு தடையும் வாராத வண்ணஞ் செய்வித்து அவ்வலங்காரத் திருப்பணியை முற்றுவித்தருளல் வேண்டும்.
translit: iṉi attiruñāṉa capaiyai alaṅkarittal vēṇṭumeṉak kuṟippitta vaṇṇam alaṅkarikkat toṭaṅkukiṉṟōm.

aruṭperuñjōti yāṇṭavarē! tēvarīr aruḷuruvāki eṅkaḷ akattum puṟattum amarntaruḷi yāṅkaḷ ceyyum ivvalaṅkārattiruppaṇiyil evvitattālum yātoru taṭaiyum vārāta vaṇṇañ ceyvittu avvalaṅkārat tiruppaṇiyai muṟṟuvittaruḷal vēṇṭum.
translation: Now, as You indicated that the holy Hall of Wisdom must be adorned, we begin to adorn it. O Lord Arut Perum Jothi! We pray that You take the form of grace, graciously abide within us and outside us, let no obstacle of any kind arise, in any way, in this holy service of adornment that we are doing, and graciously bring that holy service of adornment to completion.
commentary: Vallalar tells God that the work of adorning the holy Hall of Wisdom now begins. God had indicated that the Hall must be adorned, and the petitioners begin "as You indicated" (kuṟippitta vaṇṇam). Then he calls on Lord Arut Perum Jothi. He asks God to take the form of grace (aruḷuru) and to abide within the devotees and outside them, as God did when He caused the Hall itself to arise. He prays that this presence will let no obstacle of any kind arise, in any way, in the holy service of adornment they are doing, and that God Himself will bring that service to completion. The work is theirs to do; its completion they ask of God. When it is complete, as the next prayer asks, God is to take His seat.

sections.title: The Granting of Eternal Life

tamil: சர்வ வல்லபராகிய தனித்தலைமைக் கடவுளே! அத்திருவலங்காரத் திருப்பணி முற்றிய தருணத்தே தேவரீர் அமர்ந்தருளி அற்புதத் திருவருள் விளக்கத்தால் எங்களையும் இவ்வுலகில் இத்தேகத்தைப் பெற்ற மற்றவர்களையும் உண்மை அடியர்களாக்கி உண்மையறிவை விளக்கி, உண்மையின்பத்தை அளித்துச் சமரச சுத்த சன்மார்க்க நிலையில் வைத்துச் சத்திய வாழ்வை யடைவித்து நித்தியர்களாக்கி வாழ்வித்தல் வேண்டும்.
translit: carva vallaparākiya taṉittalaimaik kaṭavuḷē! attiruvalaṅkārat tiruppaṇi muṟṟiya taruṇattē tēvarīr amarntaruḷi aṟputat tiruvaruḷ viḷakkattāl eṅkaḷaiyum ivvulakil ittēkattaip peṟṟa maṟṟavarkaḷaiyum uṇmai aṭiyarkaḷākki uṇmaiyaṟivai viḷakki, uṇmaiyiṉpattai aḷittuc camaraca cutta caṉmārkka nilaiyil vaittuc cattiya vāḻvai yaṭaivittu nittiyarkaḷākki vāḻvittal vēṇṭum.
translation: O God of unique supremacy, the All-Powerful! When that holy service of adornment is complete, we pray that You graciously take Your seat and, by the illumination of Your wondrous grace, make us, and all others in this world who have received this body, true devotees. Illumine true knowledge in us all, grant us all true bliss, set us all in the state of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, bring us all to the true life, and make us all eternal beings who live for ever.
commentary: Calling on God as the God of unique supremacy, the All-Powerful, Vallalar asks for what is to follow the adornment. When the work is complete and God takes His seat, he asks that, by the illumination of God's wondrous grace, the petitioners and all others in this world who have received this human body be made true devotees. For all of them he asks true knowledge and true bliss, a place in the state of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, the pure path of universal harmony, the true life, and life eternal. The word for those made eternal, nittiyarkaḷ, is the plural of nittiyar, the Eternal One, a name the opening invocation gives to God. He sets no condition and makes no exception: the petition is for every human being in this world.

sections.title: Religions, the Chief Obstacle; Soul-kinship, the Chief Aim

tamil: எல்லாமுடைய அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி அற்புதக் கடவுளே! இது தொடங்கி எக்காலத்தும் சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத்தின் முக்கியத் தடையாகிய சமயங்கள், மதங்கள், மார்க்கங்கள் என்பவற்றின் ஆசார சங்கற்ப விகற்பங்களும், வருணம், ஆசிரமம் முதலிய உலகாசார சங்கற்ப விகற்பங்களும், எங்கள் மனத்திற் பற்றாதவண்ணம் அருள் செய்தல் வேண்டும். சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத்தின் முக்கிய லக்ஷியமாகிய ஆன்மநேய ஒருமைப்பாட்டுரிமை எங்களுக்குள் எக்காலத்தும் எவ்விடத்தும் எவ்விதத்தும் எவ்வளவும் விலகாமல் நிறைந்து விளங்கச் செய்வித்தருளல் வேண்டும்.
translit: ellāmuṭaiya aruṭperuñjōti aṟputak kaṭavuḷē! itu toṭaṅki ekkālattum cutta caṉmārkkattiṉ mukkiyat taṭaiyākiya camayaṅkaḷ, mataṅkaḷ, mārkkaṅkaḷ eṉpavaṟṟiṉ ācāra caṅkaṟpa vikaṟpaṅkaḷum, varuṇam, āciramam mutaliya ulakācāra caṅkaṟpa vikaṟpaṅkaḷum, eṅkaḷ maṉattiṟ paṟṟātavaṇṇam aruḷ ceytal vēṇṭum. cutta caṉmārkkattiṉ mukkiya lakṣiyamākiya āṉmanēya orumaippāṭṭurimai eṅkaḷukkuḷ ekkālattum evviṭattum evvitattum evvaḷavum vilakāmal niṟaintu viḷaṅkac ceyvittaruḷal vēṇṭum.
translation: O wondrous God, Arut Perum Jothi, who possesses all! We pray that You grant Your grace so that, from now on and for all time, the customs, notions and distinctions of the religions, sects and paths, which are the chief obstacle to Suddha Sanmarkkam, and the worldly customs, notions and distinctions such as caste and the stages of life, never take hold of our minds. We pray that You graciously make the right of oneness in soul-kinship, the chief aim of Suddha Sanmarkkam, fill and shine among us, never departing, at all times, in all places, in every way and in every measure.
commentary: Calling on the wondrous God, Arut Perum Jothi, who possesses all, Vallalar names the chief obstacle to Suddha Sanmarkkam plainly: the religions, the sects and the paths. He asks that from now on, for all time, neither their customs, notions and distinctions nor the worldly customs, notions and distinctions such as caste (varna) and the stages of life (ashrama) take hold of the petitioners' minds. Elsewhere he states his verdict in plain words. In the Arut Perum Jothi Agaval he praises Arut Perum Jothi, who made him know at the very beginning that caste, sect and religion are false. In the Great True Petition he says God made him know that caste customs and life-stage customs are false. Against the chief obstacle he sets the chief aim: Anma Neya Orumaipadu Urimai, the right of oneness that souls share through their kinship. This kinship is also the ground of Jeevakarunyam, compassion for all living beings. In his teaching on compassion he says that all living beings, created by God as parts of the one natural Truth, are brothers with one right; that is why one melts at another's suffering. He asks that this oneness fill and shine among them, always and everywhere.

sections.title: Salutations to the Divine Grace

tamil: எல்லாமாகிய தனிப் பெருந்தலைமை அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி யாண்டவரே! தேவரீர் திருவருட் பெருங்கருணைக்கு வந்தனம்! வந்தனம்!
திருச்சிற்றம்பலம்
translit: ellāmākiya taṉip peruntalaimai aruṭperuñjōti yāṇṭavarē! tēvarīr tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇaikku vantaṉam! vantaṉam!
tirucciṟṟampalam
translation: O unique Supreme Lord Arut Perum Jothi, who is all things! Salutations, salutations to the great compassion of Your divine grace!
Tiruchitrambalam.
commentary: The petition ends as it began, with names of God and with His compassion. Vallalar calls on God one last time as Lord Arut Perum Jothi, who is all things, unique and supreme. He asks for nothing more. Then comes the closing salutation, vantaṉam, said twice and offered to the great compassion of God's divine grace. The petition has told what that compassion has done. It took to heart the weariness the petitioners suffered in all those births, and placed them in this human body. By grace it made them know that there is one true God. It caused the Hall of Wisdom to arise and shine. The petition opened by calling on the God of Great Compassion; having made their petition, the petitioners close by bowing to that same compassion. As at its opening, the petition closes with Tiruchitrambalam.

works.title: The Great True Petition of the Universal Pure True Path
works.translit: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Peru Vinnappam
works.tamil: சமரச சுத்த சன்மார்க்க சத்தியப் பெரு விண்ணப்பம்

sections.title: The Great True Petition of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam

tamil: 2. சமரச சுத்த சன்மார்க்க சத்தியப் பெரு விண்ணப்பம்
திருச்சிற்றம்பலம்
translit: 2. camaraca cutta caṉmārkka cattiyap peru viṇṇappam
tirucciṟṟampalam
translation: The Great True Petition of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam. Tiruchitrambalam.
commentary: The title names this work a viṇṇappam, a petition laid before God, and calls it true (cattiya) and great (peru). It names the path: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, the Universal Pure True Path. It is popularly called the Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Peru Vinnappam, or simply the Peru Vinnappam. The printed text rests on Vallalar's own manuscript; six copies by his devotees were also found, and all of them place it second of his four prose petitions. Vallalar wrote no title on the manuscript; the editions gave it its title. Below it stands Tiruchitrambalam, "the holy small hall", the hall of the sacred dance at Chidambaram; the petition also closes with it. Like the True Petition of Wisdom, it speaks as "I" and addresses God as Tēvarīr, the most reverent word for "You". It tells what God's grace has done for Vallalar: in the darkness of ignorance before any body, in the father's seed and the mother's womb, at birth, and in infancy, boyhood and youth. God made him know that caste customs and life-stage customs are false, and that the religions, with their practices, gods and goals, are varieties of attainment within the tattvas. God gave him the good endeavour of compassion, which desires that all living beings attain bliss, and made him hold to the one path of Suddha Sanmarkkam. Again and again he asks how to know, contemplate and praise that compassion.

sections.title: From the Darkness of Ignorance into This Human Body

tamil: இயற்கை உண்மை நிறைவாகியுள்ள ஒரு சுத்த சிவானுபவ வெளியில், இயற்கைவிளக்க நிறைவாகி விளங்கிய அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி சொரூபராய், இயற்கை இன்ப நிறைவாகி ஓங்கிய சிவானந்த ஒருமைத் திருநடச்செய்கையை எல்லா உயிர்களும் இன்பமடைதற் பொருட்டுத் திருவுளக்கருணையாற் செய்தருளுகின்ற சர்வ வல்லபராகிய தனித் தலைமைக் கடவுளே! அறிவு என்பது ஒரு சிறிதுந் தோற்றாத அஞ்ஞானம் என்னும் பெரிய பாசாந்தகாரத்தில் நெடுங்காலம் சிற்றணுப்பசுவாகி அருகிக்கிடந்த அடியேனுக்குள் உள்ளொளியாகி இருந்து அப் பாசாந்தகாரத்தினின்றும் எடுத்து எல்லாப் பிறப்புடம்புகளிலும் உயர்வுடைத்தாகிய ஆறறிவுள்ள இம்மனிதப் பிறப்புடம்பில் என்னை விடுத்துச் சிறிது அறிவு விளங்கச் செய்த தேவரீரது திருவருட் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை எங்ஙனம் அறிவேன்! எவ்வாறு கருதுவேன்! என்னென்று சொல்வேன்!
translit: iyaṟkai uṇmai niṟaivākiyuḷḷa oru cutta civāṉupava veḷiyil, iyaṟkaiviḷakka niṟaivāki viḷaṅkiya aruṭperuñjōti corūparāy, iyaṟkai iṉpa niṟaivāki ōṅkiya civāṉanta orumait tirunaṭacceykaiyai ellā uyirkaḷum iṉpamaṭaitaṟ poruṭṭut tiruvuḷakkaruṇaiyāṟ ceytaruḷukiṉṟa carva vallaparākiya taṉit talaimaik kaṭavuḷē! aṟivu eṉpatu oru ciṟitun tōṟṟāta aññāṉam eṉṉum periya pācāntakārattil neṭuṅkālam ciṟṟaṇuppacuvāki arukikkiṭanta aṭiyēṉukkuḷ uḷḷoḷiyāki iruntu ap pācāntakārattiṉiṉṟum eṭuttu ellāp piṟappuṭampukaḷilum uyarvuṭaittākiya āṟaṟivuḷḷa immaṉitap piṟappuṭampil eṉṉai viṭuttuc ciṟitu aṟivu viḷaṅkac ceyta tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai eṅṅaṉam aṟivēṉ! evvāṟu karutuvēṉ! eṉṉeṉṟu colvēṉ!
translation: O God of unique supremacy, the All-Powerful! In a pure Space of Siva-experience, filled with natural truth, You are, in Your own form, Arut Perum Jothi, the Supreme Light of Grace, shining full of natural illumination; and by the compassion of Your holy heart You perform the holy dance of the oneness of Siva-bliss, rising full of natural bliss, so that all living beings may attain bliss! For a long time I, Your servant, lay dwindled as a tiny atom-soul in the great darkness of bondage called ignorance, where what is called knowledge did not appear even a little. Within me You were the inner light. You lifted me out of that darkness of bondage, placed me in this human body, which has six kinds of awareness and is the highest of all the bodies that are born, and made a little knowledge shine in me. How shall I know the power of the great compassion of Your grace, which did this! How shall I contemplate it! What shall I say of it!
commentary: Vallalar opens by naming the God to whom he speaks. He names three things, each called natural (iyaṟkai), that is, belonging to God's own nature, not made and not received from anything else. Natural truth fills the place, a pure Space of Siva-experience; Sivam, the Auspicious, is a name of God. Natural illumination shines in the form: there God is, in His own form, Arut Perum Jothi. Natural bliss rises in the act, the holy dance of the oneness of Siva-bliss. God performs that dance out of compassion, so that all living beings may attain bliss. Near the end of the petition (§25) God gives Vallalar the good endeavour of compassion (karuṇai naṉmuyaṟci) that desires the same. Jeevakarunyam, compassion for all living beings, begins in God's own compassion. Then Vallalar begins his account, before any body. For a long time he lay in the great darkness of bondage (pācāntakāram) called ignorance, a tiny atom-soul (ciṟṟaṇuppacu): pacu is the soul bound by pācam, bondage. Even there God was the inner light (uḷḷoḷi) within him. God lifted him out, placed him in this human body, the highest of all bodies that are born, and made "a little knowledge" shine in him. Vallalar claims no more than a little. Then come three questions: how shall I know, how shall I contemplate, what shall I say? They return, with small changes, as each stage of his story closes.

sections.title: In the Father's Seed

tamil: எல்லாம் வல்ல இயற்கை உண்மைக் கடவுளே! உபசாரத்தாற் பெற்ற தந்தை என்பான் ஒருவனது சுக்கிலத் துளியின்கண் என்னை ஓர் பகுதிப் பேரணு உருவிற் பெருகி வெளிப்பட இருத்திய காலத்திலும், எனக்குள் உள்ளொளியாகி இருந்து அப் பகுதிப் பேரணு உருவைச் சிருட்டித்தருளினீர். அன்றிப் புறத்தில் யாவராலும் சகிக்கப்படாத அதன் அருவருப்பையும் அசுத்தத்தையும் தீநாற்றத்தையும் சகித்து, அச்சுக்கிலத் துளியினிடத்து ஓர் ஆவியுருவாகியிருந்து, அத்துளியின்கண் உள்ள பல்வகை விரோத தத்துவங்களாற் சிறிதும் தடைபடாமல் என்னுருவையுங் காத்தருளினீர். அன்றி, அங்ஙனம் அரும்பிய ஆன்ம சத்திக் கலைகள் வெளிப்பட விளக்கி வளர்த்தும் அருளினீர்.
translit: ellām valla iyaṟkai uṇmaik kaṭavuḷē! upacārattāṟ peṟṟa tantai eṉpāṉ oruvaṉatu cukkilat tuḷiyiṉkaṇ eṉṉai ōr pakutip pēraṇu uruviṟ peruki veḷippaṭa iruttiya kālattilum, eṉakkuḷ uḷḷoḷiyāki iruntu ap pakutip pēraṇu uruvaic ciruṭṭittaruḷiṉīr. aṉṟip puṟattil yāvarālum cakikkappaṭāta ataṉ aruvaruppaiyum acuttattaiyum tīnāṟṟattaiyum cakittu, accukkilat tuḷiyiṉiṭattu ōr āviyuruvākiyiruntu, attuḷiyiṉkaṇ uḷḷa palvakai virōta tattuvaṅkaḷāṟ ciṟitum taṭaipaṭāmal eṉṉuruvaiyuṅ kāttaruḷiṉīr. aṉṟi, aṅṅaṉam arumpiya āṉma cattik kalaikaḷ veḷippaṭa viḷakki vaḷarttum aruḷiṉīr.
translation: O God of natural truth, who can do all things! You placed me in the drop of seed of a man called father, who begot me only by courtesy of speech, so that I might grow there and come forth in the form of a great atom of primal matter. Even then You were the inner light within me, and You created that atomic form. Moreover, bearing its loathsomeness, impurity and foul smell, which no one outside could bear, You were present in that drop of seed as a form of vital breath, and You protected my form too, so that the many hostile tattvas in that drop did not hinder it in the least. And You made the powers of the soul, which had budded there, come forth and shine, and You nurtured them.
commentary: Here the story enters the body, and it begins with the father. A new name of God opens the stage: the God of natural truth, who can do all things. Vallalar calls the father "a man called father, who begot me only by courtesy of speech" (upacārattāṟ peṟṟa tantai eṉpāṉ), and in the next section he names the mother in the same way. Upacāram is a courteous way of speaking: the parents are called father and mother, yet in this same passage it is God who creates his form. In the drop of seed God made a great atom of primal matter (pakutip pēraṇu) and was within it as the inner light (uḷḷoḷi), the same light that was within him in the darkness of ignorance (§2). God bore what no one outside could bear, its loathsomeness, impurity and foul smell, and stayed in that drop as a form of vital breath (āvi). Many hostile tattvas were in it; none of them could hinder his form in the least. The powers of the soul only budded there (arumpiya); God made them come forth and shine, and nurtured them. In the mother's womb, Vallalar will say, the same powers have blossomed (pūtta, §6).

sections.title: Until Joined to the Mother's Blood

tamil: உபசாரத்தாற் பெற்ற தாயென்பாள் ஒருத்தியின் சோணிதத் திரளில் என்னுருவைச் சேர்க்கும் வரையில், அப்போதப்போது என்னுருவைச் சிதைப்பதற்கு எதிரிட்ட துரிசுகள் எல்லாவற்றையும் நிக்கிரகஞ் செய்தருளினீர். இங்ஙனம் புரிந்த தேவரீரது திருவருட் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை எங்ஙனம் அறிவேன்! எவ்வாறு கருதுவேன்! என்னென்று சொல்வேன்!
translit: upacārattāṟ peṟṟa tāyeṉpāḷ oruttiyiṉ cōṇitat tiraḷil eṉṉuruvaic cērkkum varaiyil, appōtappōtu eṉṉuruvaic citaippataṟku etiriṭṭa turicukaḷ ellāvaṟṟaiyum nikkirakañ ceytaruḷiṉīr. iṅṅaṉam purinta tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai eṅṅaṉam aṟivēṉ! evvāṟu karutuvēṉ! eṉṉeṉṟu colvēṉ!
translation: Until You joined my form to the mass of blood of a woman called mother, who bore me only by courtesy of speech, You subdued, time after time, all the harmful forces that rose up to destroy my form. How shall I know the power of the great compassion of Your grace, which did all this! How shall I contemplate it! What shall I say of it!
commentary: Before his form reached the mother's womb, harmful forces (turicu) rose against it again and again to destroy it, and each time God subdued them (nikkirakam). The mother, like the father, is named "a woman called mother, who bore me only by courtesy of speech". Later Vallalar sets their care beside God's (§12, §13): the father, the mother and other living beings, guarding someone for a single moment, grow weary and break off, while God guarded him through every moment without wearying. Through this whole passage God is the one who acts: You created, You bore, You protected, You nurtured, You subdued. Vallalar is the one acted upon. The stage closes with the three questions that closed the account of the darkness of ignorance (§2): how shall I know, how shall I contemplate, what shall I say of the power of the great compassion of Your grace?

sections.title: The Atomic Form in the Mother's Womb

tamil: எல்லாம் உடைய இயற்கை விளக்கக் கடவுளே! தாய் கருப்பையில் சோணிதத் திரளில் சேர்த்து என்னை ஓர் பூதப் பேரணு உருவில் பெருகி வெளிப்பட இருத்திய காலத்திலும் எனக்குள் உள்ளொளியாகியிருந்து அப் பூதப் பேரணு உருவைச் சிருட்டித் தருளினீர். அன்றிப் புறத்தில் எவராலும் சிறிதும் சகிக்கப்படாத அதன் அசுத்தம் அருவருப்பு துற்கந்தம் முதலியவற்றைப் பொறுத்து அச்சோணிதத் திரளில் ஓர் ஆவி உருவாகியிருந்து அத்திரளினுள்ள பல்வகை விரோத தத்துவங்களால் சிறிதும் தடைபடாமல் என்னுருவைக் காத்தருளினீர்.
translit: ellām uṭaiya iyaṟkai viḷakkak kaṭavuḷē! tāy karuppaiyil cōṇitat tiraḷil cērttu eṉṉai ōr pūtap pēraṇu uruvil peruki veḷippaṭa iruttiya kālattilum eṉakkuḷ uḷḷoḷiyākiyiruntu ap pūtap pēraṇu uruvaic ciruṭṭit taruḷiṉīr. aṉṟip puṟattil evarālum ciṟitum cakikkappaṭāta ataṉ acuttam aruvaruppu tuṟkantam mutaliyavaṟṟaip poṟuttu accōṇitat tiraḷil ōr āvi uruvākiyiruntu attiraḷiṉuḷḷa palvakai virōta tattuvaṅkaḷāl ciṟitum taṭaipaṭāmal eṉṉuruvaik kāttaruḷiṉīr.
translation: O God of natural illumination, who possesses all! You joined me to the mass of blood in the mother's womb and placed me there, so that I might grow and come forth in the form of an elemental great atom. Even then You were the inner light within me, and You created that elemental atomic form. Moreover, bearing its impurity, loathsomeness, foul smell and the like, which no one outside could bear even a little, You were present in that mass of blood as a form of vital breath, and You protected my form, so that the many hostile tattvas within that mass did not hinder it in the least.
commentary: Another name of God opens this stage: the God of natural illumination, who possesses all. With the God of natural truth (§3) and, later, the God of natural bliss (§12), these names take up the three natural things of the opening address (§2). The pattern of the father's seed now repeats in the mother's womb. In the seed the form was a great atom of primal matter (pakuti); here, joined to the mother's blood, it becomes an elemental great atom (pūtap pēraṇu), an atom of the elements (pūtam) of which the body is made. Again God is the inner light within, and creates the form. Again God bears what no one outside could bear even a little, its impurity, loathsomeness and foul smell, and stays in the mass of blood as a form of vital breath (āvi). Again many hostile tattvas are present, and again they cannot hinder the form in the least. Vallalar does not hide the impurity of the womb. He names it, and with it what God bore for one small life.

sections.title: Harmful Forces Subdued, the Soul's Powers Nurtured

tamil: அன்றியும் அவ்விடத்து எதிரிட்ட துரிசுகள் எல்லாவற்றையும் நிக்கிரகஞ் செய்தருளினீர். அன்றி அங்ஙனம் பூத்த ஆன்ம சத்திக் கலைகள் வாட்டமடையாது வெளிப்பட்டு விளங்க வளர்த்தருளினீர்.
translit: aṉṟiyum avviṭattu etiriṭṭa turicukaḷ ellāvaṟṟaiyum nikkirakañ ceytaruḷiṉīr. aṉṟi aṅṅaṉam pūtta āṉma cattik kalaikaḷ vāṭṭamaṭaiyātu veḷippaṭṭu viḷaṅka vaḷarttaruḷiṉīr.
translation: Moreover, You subdued all the harmful forces that rose up there. And You nurtured the powers of the soul that had blossomed there, so that they came forth and shone without withering.
commentary: Two more acts of God belong to the stage of the elemental atom. First, the harmful forces (turicu) that rose against the new life there, God subdued (nikkirakam), as He had subdued those that rose against it before it reached the mother (§4). The forces rose; God held them down. Second, the powers of the soul (āṉma cattik kalaikaḷ), which had only budded in the father's seed (§3), have now blossomed (pūtta), and God nurtured them so that they came forth and shone without withering. Vallalar tells the growth of the soul's powers in the same steps as the growth of the body: budded in the seed, blossomed in the womb, and kept from withering. At every step the act is God's: ceytaruḷiṉīr, vaḷarttaruḷiṉīr, "You graciously did", "You graciously nurtured".

sections.title: From Atomic Form to Bodily Form

tamil: அன்றியும் தாய் கருப்பையினிடத்துப் பூதப் பேரணு உருவில் கிடந்த என்னை அக்கருப்பையில் பவுதிக பிண்ட வடிவில் இருத்தும் வரையில் நச்சுக்கிருமி நச்சுக்காற்று நச்சுச்சுவாலை முதலிய உற்பாத வகைகளால் எனது பூதப்பேரணு உருச்சிதறி வேறுபடாமலும் காத்தருளினீர். அன்றியும் தாய் கருப்பையில் பவுதிக பிண்ட வடிவில் என்னை இருத்திய காலத்திலும் எனது இச்சை ஞானக் கிரியைகளை வெளிப்படுத்துதல் முதலிய உபகரிப்பு அதிகரிப்புகளுக்கு உரிய உபயோக தத்துவ உறுப்புகள் எல்லாவற்றையும் குறைவின்றி வகுத்தமைத்து வளர்த்துக் காத்தருளினீர்.
translit: aṉṟiyum tāy karuppaiyiṉiṭattup pūtap pēraṇu uruvil kiṭanta eṉṉai akkaruppaiyil pavutika piṇṭa vaṭivil iruttum varaiyil naccukkirumi naccukkāṟṟu naccuccuvālai mutaliya uṟpāta vakaikaḷāl eṉatu pūtappēraṇu uruccitaṟi vēṟupaṭāmalum kāttaruḷiṉīr. aṉṟiyum tāy karuppaiyil pavutika piṇṭa vaṭivil eṉṉai iruttiya kālattilum eṉatu iccai ñāṉak kiriyaikaḷai veḷippaṭuttutal mutaliya upakarippu atikarippukaḷukku uriya upayōka tattuva uṟuppukaḷ ellāvaṟṟaiyum kuṟaiviṉṟi vakuttamaittu vaḷarttuk kāttaruḷiṉīr.
translation: Moreover, while I lay in the mother's womb in the form of an elemental great atom, until You set me in that womb in the physical form of an embryo, You also protected that elemental atomic form of mine, so that calamities such as poisonous germs, poisonous air and poisonous flame did not scatter it or change it. Moreover, even when You had placed me in the mother's womb in the physical form of an embryo, You shaped and arranged, without any lack, all the serviceable organs of the tattvas needed to aid and to increase such workings as the bringing forth of my desire, knowledge and action; and You nurtured them and protected them.
commentary: This section follows the form from the elemental atom to the body. Until the elemental great atom became a physical embryo (pavutika piṇṭa vaṭivu), it could have been scattered and changed by calamities (uṟpātam): poisonous germs, poisonous air, poisonous flame. God kept the form whole through all of them. Then, once the embryo had a physical form, God built in it the organs it would need. Vallalar calls them the serviceable organs of the tattvas (upayōka tattuva uṟuppukaḷ): the parts and faculties built from the tattvas, the principles of which body and mind are made. They serve to aid and to increase such workings as the bringing forth of the soul's desire, knowledge and action (iccai, ñāṉam, kiriyai), the three powers by which a soul desires, knows and acts. God shaped them, arranged them, left none of them lacking, and then nurtured and protected them, all while he still lay in the womb.

sections.title: Relief from the Confinement of the Womb

tamil: அன்றியும் அடியேன் தாய் கருப்பையில் பிண்ட வடிவில் கிடந்த காலத்து இரும்பில் பெரிதும் கடினமுடையதாய் இருட்குகையில் பெரிதும் இருளுடையதாய் மிகவும் சிற்றளவுடையதாய் அசுத்தம் முதலியவற்றால் நிரம்பிய அக்கருப்பையினுள் நெருக்கத்தாலும் வெப்பத்தாலும் புழுங்கிய புழுக்கத்தினால் வருந்தி வருந்திக் களைத்தபோ தெல்லாம் அங்ஙனம் அமுதக் காற்றை அடிக்கடி மெல்லென வீசுவித்து அவ்வருத்தமும் களைப்பும் தவிர்த்துக் காத்தருளினீர்.
translit: aṉṟiyum aṭiyēṉ tāy karuppaiyil piṇṭa vaṭivil kiṭanta kālattu irumpil peritum kaṭiṉamuṭaiyatāy iruṭkukaiyil peritum iruḷuṭaiyatāy mikavum ciṟṟaḷavuṭaiyatāy acuttam mutaliyavaṟṟāl nirampiya akkaruppaiyiṉuḷ nerukkattālum veppattālum puḻuṅkiya puḻukkattiṉāl varunti varuntik kaḷaittapō tellām aṅṅaṉam amutak kāṟṟai aṭikkaṭi melleṉa vīcuvittu avvaruttamum kaḷaippum tavirttuk kāttaruḷiṉīr.
translation: Moreover, when I, Your servant, lay in the form of an embryo in the mother's womb, that womb was far harder than iron, far darker than a dark cave, very small, and filled with impurity and the like. Whenever I suffered again and again and grew faint in the stifling closeness and heat inside it, You made a breeze of nectar blow there softly and often, took away that suffering and faintness, and protected me.
commentary: Vallalar describes the womb from inside, as the one who lay there, and he calls himself aṭiyēṉ, Your servant, the word he used of himself in the darkness of ignorance (§2). The womb is far harder than iron, far darker than a dark cave, very small, and full of impurity. Pressed and heated, he suffered again and again (varunti varunti) and grew faint. Each time, God made a breeze of nectar (amutak kāṟṟu) blow softly within that closed place and took the suffering and the faintness away. The verb is causative (vīcuvittu, "made it blow"): the breeze came from God. The relief came often (aṭikkaṭi) and gently (melleṉa), as the child needed it, and the section ends, as §5 and §7 do: You protected me.

sections.title: Hunger, Fear and Danger in the Womb

tamil: அன்றியும் தாய் கருப்பையில் பிண்ட வடிவில் கிடந்து பசியினால் பரதவித்து மூர்ச்சித்த போதெல்லாம் பூதகாரிய அமுதத்தை எனக்கு ஊட்டுவித்துப் பசியை நீக்கி மூர்ச்சை தெளிவித் தருளினீர். அன்றியும் தாய் கருப்பையில் பிண்ட வடிவில் கிடந்து பேய்வெருட்டாலும் பேரிருட்டாலும் பயந்த போதெல்லாம் நாத ஒலியால் பேய் வெருட்டையும் விந்து விளக்கத்தால் பேரிருட்டையும் தவிர்த்து என் பயத்தை நீக்கியருளினீர், அன்றி தாய் கருப்பையின்கண் நேரிட்ட பெருந்தீ பெருங்காற்று பேரோசை பெருவெள்ளம் பெரும்புழு முதலிய உற்பாத துரிசுகள் அனைத்தையும் தவிர்த்துக் காத்து அப்பிண்ட வடிவில் எனக்கு ஓரறிவையும் விளக்கி அருளினீர்.
translit: aṉṟiyum tāy karuppaiyil piṇṭa vaṭivil kiṭantu paciyiṉāl paratavittu mūrccitta pōtellām pūtakāriya amutattai eṉakku ūṭṭuvittup paciyai nīkki mūrccai teḷivit taruḷiṉīr. aṉṟiyum tāy karuppaiyil piṇṭa vaṭivil kiṭantu pēyveruṭṭālum pēriruṭṭālum payanta pōtellām nāta oliyāl pēy veruṭṭaiyum vintu viḷakkattāl pēriruṭṭaiyum tavirttu eṉ payattai nīkkiyaruḷiṉīr, aṉṟi tāy karuppaiyiṉkaṇ nēriṭṭa peruntī peruṅkāṟṟu pērōcai peruveḷḷam perumpuḻu mutaliya uṟpāta turicukaḷ aṉaittaiyum tavirttuk kāttu appiṇṭa vaṭivil eṉakku ōraṟivaiyum viḷakki aruḷiṉīr.
translation: Moreover, whenever I lay in the form of an embryo in the mother's womb and fainted, tormented by hunger, You had me fed with nectar formed of the elements, took away my hunger, and revived me from my faint. Moreover, whenever I lay in the form of an embryo in the mother's womb and was afraid, terrified by ghosts and by the great darkness, You drove away the terror of ghosts by the sound of Nada, the primal sound, and the great darkness by the light of Bindu, and took away my fear. And You warded off all the calamitous harms that came upon me in the mother's womb, such as great fire, great wind, great noise, great flood and great worms, protected me, and in that embryonic form You made one kind of awareness shine in me.
commentary: Hunger reached him even in the womb, so sharply that he was tormented (paratavittu) and fainted. Each time, God had him fed (ūṭṭuvittu) with nectar formed of the elements (pūtakāriya amutam), the nourishment of a body made of the elements, took the hunger away and brought him out of the faint. Even this nourishment, which seems to come by itself, he receives as God's own feeding. In Vallalar's teaching of Jeevakarunyam, compassion for all living beings, relieving hunger stands first; here he finds God relieving his own hunger before he was born. Fear came next. In the darkness of the womb he was terrified by ghosts (pēy) and by the great darkness. God answered each with its opposite: against the terror, the sound of Nada (nāta oli); against the darkness, the light of Bindu (vintu viḷakkam). Nada and Bindu are among the highest of the tattvas; here Vallalar names the one as sound and the other as light. Then come the calamities of the womb, each called great: great fire, great wind, great noise, great flood, great worms. God warded off every one. Last, in that embryonic form God made one kind of awareness (ōraṟivu) shine in him, the first of the six kinds of awareness that the human body has (§2).

sections.title: Good Things Prepared for Life in the World

tamil: அன்றியும் உலகினிடத்தே பிறந்து அனுபவிப்பதற்குரிய சுபஅனுபவப் பெருக்கம் ஆயுட் பெருக்கம் முதலிய நன்மைகளையும் எனக்கு அப்பிண்ட வடிவின்கண்ணே அமைத்தருளினீர்.
translit: aṉṟiyum ulakiṉiṭattē piṟantu aṉupavippataṟkuriya cupa-aṉupavap perukkam āyuṭ perukkam mutaliya naṉmaikaḷaiyum eṉakku appiṇṭa vaṭiviṉkaṇṇē amaittaruḷiṉīr.
translation: Moreover, in that very embryonic form You set in place for me the good things to be enjoyed when I was born into the world, such as an abundance of auspicious experience and an abundance of life-span.
commentary: While he still lay in the womb, God had already prepared the life to come. In that very embryonic form (appiṇṭa vaṭiviṉkaṇṇē) God set in place for him the good things he would enjoy once he was born into the world: an abundance of auspicious experience (cupa aṉupavam), an abundance of life-span (āyuḷ), and others with them. The closing ē of kaṇṇē stresses the point: in that very form, before birth. The opening "moreover" (aṉṟiyum) adds this gift to all that God had already done in the womb: creating the form and guarding it, forming its organs, relieving its heat and hunger, removing its fear and lighting its first awareness (sections 5 to 9). How much good a life will hold, and how long it will last, Vallalar receives as God's gift, laid down before the child has drawn a breath in the world.

sections.title: Protection During Birth

tamil: அன்றியும் சோணிதக்காற்றின் அடிபடல் யோனி நெருக்குண்ணல் முதலிய அவத்தைகளால் அபாயம் நேரிட ஒட்டாமற் காத்து இவ்வுலகினிடத்தே தோற்றுவித்தருளினீர். இங்ஙனம் புரிந்த தேவரீரது திருவருட் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை எங்ஙனம் அறிவேன்! எவ்வாறு கருதுவேன்! என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
translit: aṉṟiyum cōṇitakkāṟṟiṉ aṭipaṭal yōṉi nerukkuṇṇal mutaliya avattaikaḷāl apāyam nēriṭa oṭṭāmaṟ kāttu ivvulakiṉiṭattē tōṟṟuvittaruḷiṉīr. iṅṅaṉam purinta tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai eṅṅaṉam aṟivēṉ! evvāṟu karutuvēṉ! eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
translation: Moreover, You guarded me so that no danger came to me from such ordeals as the blows of the wind of the blood and the pressing of the birth passage, and You brought me forth into this world. How shall I know the power of the great compassion of Your grace, which did all this! How shall I contemplate it! How shall I praise it!
commentary: Birth itself is an ordeal (avattai). Vallalar names two: the blows of the wind of the blood (cōṇitak kāṟṟu) and the pressing of the birth passage. God did not let danger come of them; He guarded him and brought him forth into this world. With birth, the account that began in section 5 with the call to the God of natural illumination comes to its close. In the womb God created his form, bore its impurity, guarded it from hostile tattvas, harmful forces and calamities, formed its organs, relieved its heat and hunger, removed its fear, lit its first awareness and prepared its life in the world. Now He brings it into the world. Vallalar closes the whole account as he closed the darkness of ignorance (section 2) and the father's seed (section 4), with three questions, and this time the third is praise: how shall he praise it? A footnote in the Urainadai editions compares this passage with Manikkavasagar's Potri Tiruvakaval in the Tiruvasagam, which also counts, month by month, the dangers survived in the mother's womb.

sections.title: No Father's Care Can Compare

tamil: எல்லாமாகிய இயற்கை இன்பக் கடவுளே! தந்தை என்பவனது சுக்கிலப் பையின்கண் யான் வந்தமைந்த கணப்போது தொடங்கி தாய் என்பவளது சோணிதப் பையின்கண் சென்றடைந்த கணப்போதிற்கு முன்கணப்போது வரையுமாக என்னால் ஒருவாறு அளவிடப்பட்ட ஒரு கோடி ஒன்பது லக்ஷத்து அறுபதினாயிரம் கணப்போது பரியந்தம் எவ்வகைத் தடைகளும் வாராதபடி, பகுதிப் பேரணு உருவிற்கிடந்த எனது அகத்தினும் புறத்தினும் அருவாகியும் உருவாகியும் சலித்தல் முதலிய இன்றி அன்பொடும் அருளொடும் பாதுகாத்திருந்த தேவரீரது திருவருட்பெருங்கருணைத் தன்மைக்கு இவ்வுலகில் ஒருவாறு ஒருகணப்போது பாதுகாத்தலில் சலிப்படைந்தும் தளர்ச்சியடைந்தும் அருவருப்புற்றும் சுதந்தரமற்றும் பராக்கிலிருந்தும் தடைபடுகின்ற தந்தை முதலிய ஜீவர்கள் கருணைத் தன்மையை ஒப்பென்று சொல்வதற்கு எவ்விதத்தினும் சிறிதாயினும் மனம் துணியாமையால் அங்ஙனம் உபசரியாதவனாகி இருக்கின்றேன். ஆகலில் தேவரீரது திருவருட் பெருங்கருணையை என்னென்று கருதுவேன்! என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
translit: ellāmākiya iyaṟkai iṉpak kaṭavuḷē! tantai eṉpavaṉatu cukkilap paiyiṉkaṇ yāṉ vantamainta kaṇappōtu toṭaṅki tāy eṉpavaḷatu cōṇitap paiyiṉkaṇ ceṉṟaṭainta kaṇappōtiṟku muṉkaṇappōtu varaiyumāka eṉṉāl oruvāṟu aḷaviṭappaṭṭa oru kōṭi oṉpatu lakṣattu aṟupatiṉāyiram kaṇappōtu pariyantam evvakait taṭaikaḷum vārātapaṭi, pakutip pēraṇu uruviṟkiṭanta eṉatu akattiṉum puṟattiṉum aruvākiyum uruvākiyum calittal mutaliya iṉṟi aṉpoṭum aruḷoṭum pātukāttirunta tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭperuṅkaruṇait taṉmaikku ivvulakil oruvāṟu orukaṇappōtu pātukāttalil calippaṭaintum taḷarcciyaṭaintum aruvaruppuṟṟum cutantaramaṟṟum parākkiliruntum taṭaipaṭukiṉṟa tantai mutaliya jīvarkaḷ karuṇait taṉmaiyai oppeṉṟu colvataṟku evvitattiṉum ciṟitāyiṉum maṉam tuṇiyāmaiyāl aṅṅaṉam upacariyātavaṉāki irukkiṉṟēṉ. ākalil tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇaiyai eṉṉeṉṟu karutuvēṉ! eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
translation: O God of natural bliss, who are all things! From the moment I came and settled in the seminal sac of the one called father until the moment before I reached the blood-sac of the one called mother, a span I have reckoned in some fashion at ten million, nine hundred and sixty thousand moments, You guarded me, as I lay in the atomic form of primal matter, within and without, as the formless and as form, without wearying or the like, with love and with grace, so that no hindrance of any kind came to me. In this world the father and other living beings, guarding someone in some fashion for a single moment, grow weary, grow faint, feel disgust, lack freedom, become distracted, and break off. My mind does not dare in any way, even a little, to call their compassion equal to the great compassion of Your grace; so I have remained one who will not say so, even as a courtesy. Therefore, how shall I contemplate the great compassion of Your grace! How shall I praise it!
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as the God of natural bliss, who is all things. With the God of natural truth (section 3) and of natural illumination (section 5), this completes the three names that echo the petition's opening (section 2). From the moment he came into the father's seminal sac until the moment before he reached the mother's blood-sac, he counts, "in some fashion", ten million, nine hundred and sixty thousand moments (kaṇappōtu). Through every one of them God guarded him as he lay in the atomic form of primal matter, within and without, as the formless and as form, without wearying, with love and with grace (aṉpoṭum aruḷoṭum). Beside this he sets the care of the father and other living beings. Guarding someone for a single moment, they grow weary, grow faint, feel disgust, lack freedom, become distracted, and break off. His mind does not dare call their compassion equal to God's, in any way, even a little. In sections 3 and 4 he called his parents father and mother only by courtesy (upacāram). Here he withholds that courtesy from their compassion: he will not call it equal to God's even as a figure of speech. Against one moment of human care stand millions of moments of God's unbroken care, and he can only ask how to contemplate it and how to praise it.

sections.title: No Mother's Care Can Compare

tamil: அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதித் தனித்தலைமைக் கடவுளே! தாய் என்பவளது சோணிதப் பையின்கண் யான் வந்தமைந்த கணப்போது தொடங்கி இவ்வுலகில் தோன்றிய கணப்போதிற்கு முன்கணப்போது வரையுமாக என்னால் ஒருவாறு அளவிடப்பட்ட ஆறுகோடி நாற்பத்தெட்டு லக்ஷங் கணப்போது பரியந்தம் எவ்வகைத் தடைகளும் எவ்வகை ஆபத்துகளும் வாராதபடி பூதப்பேரணு உருவிலும் பிண்டப் பெரு வடிவிலும் கிடந்த எனது அகத்தினும் புறத்தினும் அருவாகியும் உருவாகியும் சலித்தல் முதலிய இன்றிப் பெருந்தயவினோடு பாதுகாத்திருந்த தேவரீரது திருவருட் பெருங்கருணைத் தன்மைக்கு இவ்வுலகில் ஒருவாறு ஒரு கணப்போது பாதுகாத்தலிற் சலித்தும் தளர்ந்தும் அருவருத்தும் பரதந்திரித்தும் பராக்கடைந்தும் தடைபடுகின்ற தாய் முதலிய ஜீவர் கருணைத் தன்மையை ஒப்பென்று சொல்வதற்கு எவ்வகையினும் எத்துணையும் மனம் துணியாமையால் அங்ஙனம் உபசரியாதவனாகி இருக்கின்றேன். ஆகலில் தேவரீரது திருவருட் பெருங்கருணையை என்னென்று கருதுவேன்! எங்ஙனம் துதிப்பேன்!
translit: aruṭperuñjōtit taṉittalaimaik kaṭavuḷē! tāy eṉpavaḷatu cōṇitap paiyiṉkaṇ yāṉ vantamainta kaṇappōtu toṭaṅki ivvulakil tōṉṟiya kaṇappōtiṟku muṉkaṇappōtu varaiyumāka eṉṉāl oruvāṟu aḷaviṭappaṭṭa āṟukōṭi nāṟpatteṭṭu lakṣaṅ kaṇappōtu pariyantam evvakait taṭaikaḷum evvakai āpattukaḷum vārātapaṭi pūtappēraṇu uruvilum piṇṭap peru vaṭivilum kiṭanta eṉatu akattiṉum puṟattiṉum aruvākiyum uruvākiyum calittal mutaliya iṉṟip peruntayaviṉōṭu pātukāttirunta tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇait taṉmaikku ivvulakil oruvāṟu oru kaṇappōtu pātukāttaliṟ calittum taḷarntum aruvaruttum paratantirittum parākkaṭaintum taṭaipaṭukiṉṟa tāy mutaliya jīvar karuṇait taṉmaiyai oppeṉṟu colvataṟku evvakaiyiṉum ettuṇaiyum maṉam tuṇiyāmaiyāl aṅṅaṉam upacariyātavaṉāki irukkiṉṟēṉ. ākalil tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇaiyai eṉṉeṉṟu karutuvēṉ! eṅṅaṉam tutippēṉ!
translation: O Arut Perum Jothi, God of unique supremacy!
