From the moment I came and settled in the blood-sac of the one called mother until the moment before I appeared in this world, a span I have reckoned in some fashion at sixty-four million, eight hundred thousand moments, You guarded me, as I lay in the elemental atomic form and in the great form of the embryo, within and without, as the formless and as form, without wearying or the like, with great kindness, so that no hindrance of any kind and no danger of any kind came to me. In this world the mother and other living beings, guarding someone in some fashion for a single moment, grow weary, grow faint, feel disgust, depend on others, become distracted, and break off. My mind does not dare in any way, to any degree, to call their compassion equal to the great compassion of Your grace; so I have remained one who will not say so, even as a courtesy. Therefore, how shall I contemplate the great compassion of Your grace! How shall I praise it!
commentary: Now Vallalar calls on God as Arut Perum Jothi, the God of unique supremacy, and measures the second stage. From the moment he came to rest in the mother's blood-sac until the moment before he appeared in this world, he reckons, in some fashion, sixty-four million, eight hundred thousand moments (kaṇappōtu). Through all of them, while he lay in the elemental atomic form (pūtap pēraṇu) and in the great form of the embryo (piṇṭam), God guarded him within and without, as the formless and as form, without wearying, with great kindness (peruntayavu), so that no hindrance and no danger of any kind came to him. Then, as he did for the father, he names how the care of the mother and other living beings falls short. Guarding someone for a single moment, they grow weary, grow faint, feel disgust, depend on others, become distracted, and break off. So his mind does not dare, to any degree, call their compassion equal to God's, and he will not say so even as a courtesy. Section 12 measured God's care in the father's seed; this section measures it in the mother's womb. Both end with the same two questions: how shall he contemplate the great compassion of God's grace, and how shall he praise it?

sections.title: Drawn Out of the Great Darkness in a Moment

tamil: யாவராலும் பிரித்தற்கு ஒருவாற்றானும் கூடாத பாசம் என்னும் மகாந்தகாரத்தில் யான் அது என்னும் பேதந் தோன்றாது அருகிக் கலந்து அளவிறந்த காலம் முன்பின் என்பதின்றி மூர்ச்சித்துக் கிடந்த என்னை அம்மகாந்தகாரத்தி னின்றும் ஒரு கணப்பொழுதினுள் அதிகாரணக் கிரியையால் அதிகாரணப் பகுதி உருவில் பிரித்தெடுத்தருளிய தேவரீரது திருவருட் பேராற்றலை என்னென்று கருதி என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
translit: yāvarālum pirittaṟku oruvāṟṟāṉum kūṭāta pācam eṉṉum makāntakārattil yāṉ atu eṉṉum pētan tōṉṟātu arukik kalantu aḷaviṟanta kālam muṉpiṉ eṉpatiṉṟi mūrccittuk kiṭanta eṉṉai ammakāntakāratti ṉiṉṟum oru kaṇappoḻutiṉuḷ atikāraṇak kiriyaiyāl atikāraṇap pakuti uruvil piritteṭuttaruḷiya tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ pērāṟṟalai eṉṉeṉṟu karuti eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
translation: I lay in the great darkness called bondage, from which no one could in any way separate me. Shrunken and mingled with it, so that no difference between "I" and "it" appeared, I lay in a swoon for time beyond measure, with no before and no after. Within a single moment, by supra-causal action, You separated me out of that great darkness and drew me forth in a supra-causal form of primal matter. How shall I contemplate, how shall I praise the great power of Your grace!
commentary: This section has no call to God of its own. It follows the praise that closes section 13 and turns from God's compassion to God's power (pērāṟṟal). Vallalar goes back to the state before any body. He lay in the great darkness called pācam, bondage, for time beyond measure, with no before and no after. He was so shrunken and mingled with it that no difference between "I" and "it" appeared, and he lay in a swoon. No one, he says, could in any way separate him from it. God did it within a single moment, by supra-causal action (atikāraṇak kiriyai), separating him out of the darkness in a supra-causal form of pakuti, primal matter. This is the first of the forms through which he would pass; the next section follows him through the rest. Section 2 spoke of the same darkness: there he lay shrunken, a tiny atom-soul, in the great darkness of bondage called ignorance, until God, as the inner light within him, lifted him out and placed him in this human body.

sections.title: From Causal Form to This Body in a Moment

tamil: சத்திய ஞானானந்தத் தனித்தலைமைக் கடவுளே! காரணக் கிரியையால் காரணப்பகுதி உருவினும், அதிசூக்குமக் கிரியையால் அதிசூக்குமப் பகுதி உருவினும், சூக்குமக் கிரியையால் சூக்குமப்பகுதி உருவினும், பரத்துவ சத்திசத்தரால் பூத உருவினும், அபரத்துவ சத்திசத்தரால் பவுதிக வடிவினும் ஒரு கணப்போதினுள் என்னைச் செலுத்தாமற் செலுத்திய தேவரீரது திருவருட் பேராற்றலை என்னென்று கருதி என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
translit: cattiya ñāṉāṉantat taṉittalaimaik kaṭavuḷē! kāraṇak kiriyaiyāl kāraṇappakuti uruviṉum, aticūkkumak kiriyaiyāl aticūkkumap pakuti uruviṉum, cūkkumak kiriyaiyāl cūkkumappakuti uruviṉum, parattuva catticattarāl pūta uruviṉum, aparattuva catticattarāl pavutika vaṭiviṉum oru kaṇappōtiṉuḷ eṉṉaic celuttāmaṟ celuttiya tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ pērāṟṟalai eṉṉeṉṟu karuti eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
translation: O God of unique supremacy, who are true Wisdom and Bliss! By causal action You moved me into a causal form of primal matter; by ultra-subtle action, into an ultra-subtle form of primal matter; by subtle action, into a subtle form of primal matter; through the higher energies and their agents, into a form of the elements; and through the lower energies and their agents, into the physical form. All this You did within a single moment, moving me without moving me. How shall I contemplate, how shall I praise the great power of Your grace!
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as the God of unique supremacy who is true Wisdom and Bliss. Section 14 drew him out of bondage in a supra-causal form. This section names the forms that followed, step by step, each with its own means. By causal action God moved him into a causal form, by ultra-subtle action into an ultra-subtle form, and by subtle action into a subtle form; each of these is a form of pakuti, primal matter. Then the means change. Through the higher energies and their agents (parattuva catti cattar) he came into a form of the elements (pūtam). Through the lower energies and their agents (aparattuva catti cattar) he came into the physical form (pavutika vaṭivu). Vallalar says all of this happened within a single moment. And he says God moved him "without moving" him (celuttāmaṟ celuttiya). He leaves the paradox as it stands. Section 16 has the same turn of phrase, where God, standing within, makes the whole body appear without appearing.

sections.title: All the Parts of This Body, Within and without

tamil: அகண்ட பூரணானந்தராகிய அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதிக் கடவுளே! ஜீவனை ஆதரிப்பிக்கும் பூதப் பிருதிவித் தோற்றமும், ஜீவனை விருத்தி செய்விக்கும் பூத நீர்த் தோற்றமும், ஜீவனை விளக்கஞ் செய்விக்கும் பூதாக்கினித் தோற்றமும், ஜீவனை அதிகரிப்பிக்கும் பூத வாயுத் தோற்றமும், ஜீவனை வியாபகஞ் செய்விக்கும் பூத வெளித் தோற்றமும், உபப்பிருதிவி உபநீர் உபாக்கினி உபவாயு முதலிய தோற்றங்களும், அவைகள் இருக்கும் இடங்களும், தொழிலிடம் முதலிய இடங்களும், ஒலி அறிவு, உருவ அறிவு, சுவை அறிவு, நாற்ற அறிவு, பரிச அறிவு என்னும் ஐவகைக் குணஅறிவுகளும், அவைகள் இருத்தற்குரிய செவி கண் நாக்கு மூக்கு மெய் என்னும் உள்ளிடப் பொறிகளும், அவைகள் உத்தியோகித்தற்குரிய வெளியிடப் பொறிகளும், வசனித்தறிதல் நடந்தறிதல் கொடுத்தெடுத் தறிதல் மலம் விடுத்தறிதல் சலம் விடுத்தறிதல் என்னும் ஐவகைத் தொழிலறிவுகளும், அவைகள் இருத்தற்குரிய வாக்கு பாதம் கை நீர்வாயில் அபானவாயில் என்னும் கரும உள்ளிடப் பொறிகளும், அவைகள் தொழிற்படற் குரிய கருமப் புறவிடப்பொறிகளும், நினைத்தல் விசாரித்தல் நிச்சயித்தல் அகங்கரித்தல் என்னும் சூக்குமக் கரணத் தொழில்களும், அவைகளை இயற்றும் மனம், புத்தி, சித்தம், அகங்காரம் என்னும் சூக்கும கரணங்களும், அவைகளை இயற்றுவிக்கும் அதிசூக்கும கரணங்களும் அக்கரணங்களின் உபகரணங்களாகிப் பலபல பேதப்பட்டு விரிந்த சத்துவம், ராஜசம், தாமச முதலிய குணங்களும், அவைகள் translation: O God Arut Perum Jothi, who are undivided, complete Bliss! There is the appearance of earth as an element, which supports the soul; of water as an element, which makes the soul grow; of fire as an element, which makes the soul shine; of air as an element, which makes the soul increase; and of space as an element, which makes the soul pervade. There are the appearances of secondary earth, secondary water, secondary fire, secondary air and the rest, with the places where they dwell and places such as their places of work. There are the five kinds of knowing through qualities: knowing sound, knowing form, knowing taste, knowing smell and knowing touch; the inner organs in which they dwell, called ear, eye, tongue, nose and body; and the outer organs through which they work. There are the five kinds of knowing through action: knowing by speaking, knowing by walking, knowing by giving and taking, knowing by voiding excrement and knowing by voiding urine; the inner organs of action in which they dwell, called speech, feet, hands, the urinary opening and the anal opening; and the outer organs of action through which they act. There are the actions of the subtle instruments, called thinking, considering, deciding and asserting "I"; the subtle instruments that perform them, called mind, intellect, the reflecting mind and the sense of "I"; the ultra-subtle instruments that set those to work; and the qualities, sattva, rajas, tamas and the rest, which serve those instruments as their aids and branch out into many, many kinds, with the places where they dwell and work. There are the intermediate actions, such as bringing to maturity, making fit, desiring, discerning, ruling, causing and effecting; the instruments at work while these are performed, such as union, desire and knowledge; the places that belong to those instruments; and the places where they work. There are the higher actions, such as causing impurity to be removed, causing happiness to be desired, causing purity, being the way to attain bliss and being a help; the tattvas that perform them; the places where they dwell; and the places from which they give the impulse. There are the chief actions, such as knowing, making known, experiencing and causing to experience; the energies and their agents that perform them; the places where they dwell; and the places where they hold sway. There are the workings of wind, bile and phlegm, with the places where they dwell and the places where they work. There are the energies, such as the energy of the sun, the energy of the moon, the energy of fire, the energy of the stars, the energy of Brahma, the energy of Maya and the energy of Rudra, with the places where they dwell and hold sway; and the agents who run those energies, with the places where they dwell and hold sway. There are the states, such as waking, dreaming and deep sleep, with the places where they dwell. And in this way there are many, many more inner organs and inner-outer organs. There are the kinds of skin, such as the outer skin, the covering skin, the tough skin and the soft skin; the kinds of nerve, such as white, red, green, small and large nerves; the kinds of bone, such as large, small, long and bent bones; the kinds of blood, such as good blood, poor blood, mixed blood and tawny blood; the kinds of flesh, such as soft, hard, earthy and watery flesh; the kinds of seed, such as the upper and the lower; the kinds of brain, such as the Ōṅkāra brain and the Āṅkāra brain; and the kinds of nectar, such as the nectar of the head and the nectar of the middle. There are the kinds of colour, called white, red, green, black and gold, and the kinds of blended colour, called red in white, green in white, black in white and gold in white; white in red, green in red, black in red and gold in red; white in green, red in green, gold in green and black in green; white in black, red in black, green in black and gold in black; white in gold, red in gold, green in gold and black in gold. There are the places where each of these dwells, their kinds of action and their kinds of use. And in this way there are many, many more outer organs and outer-outer organs. All these, to serve me, You made appear together within this physical form: standing within, You made them appear, and standing within, You did not appear. How shall I know, how shall I contemplate, how shall I praise the great power of Your grace!
commentary: This section is one long sentence in the Tamil. It calls on Arut Perum Jothi, undivided, complete Bliss, and lists all that God made appear within this physical body; its verb and its cry of praise come only at the close. The list moves from within to without. First come the five elements (pūtam), each named with what it does for the soul (jīvaṉ): earth supports it, water makes it grow, fire makes it shine, air makes it increase, space makes it pervade. Then come the secondary elements; five kinds of knowing through qualities, with their inner and outer organs; and five kinds of knowing through action. Even speaking, walking, giving and taking, and voiding excrement and urine he calls a knowing (aṟital). Then come the subtle instruments (karaṇam), mind, intellect, cittam and akaṅkāram, with the ultra-subtle instruments behind them and the qualities (kuṇam) that serve them; the intermediate actions; and the higher actions, such as causing impurity to be removed and being the way to bliss, with the tattvas that perform them. Then come the chief actions of knowing and experiencing, done by energies and their agents (catti cattar); wind, bile and phlegm; the energies of the sun, moon, fire and stars, and of Brahma, Maya and Rudra, with the agents who run them; and the states of waking, dreaming and deep sleep. These he counts as inner and inner-outer organs. Last come the outer and outer-outer organs: skin, nerve, bone, blood, flesh, seed, brain and nectar, and five colours with their twenty blends. All of it God made appear together to serve him, standing within and not appearing. Section 15 has the same turn of phrase: God moved him without moving him. He can only ask how to know, contemplate and praise that power.

sections.title: Born Human, in a Place Where Good Qualities Grow

tamil: சுத்த சன்மார்க்க லக்ஷிய சத்திய ஞானக் கடவுளே! ஜீவர்களாற் கணித்தறியப்படாத பெரிய உலகின்கண்ணே, பேராசை பெருங்கோபம் பெருமோகம் பெருமதம் பெருலோபம் பேரழுக்காறு பேரகங்காரம் பெருவயிரம் பெருமடம் பெருமயக்கம் முதலிய பெருங்குற்றங்களே பெரும்பாலும் விளைவதற்குரிமையாகிய மற்றை இடங்களிற் பிறப்பியாமல், குணங்களே பெரும்பாலும் விளைதற்குரிய இவ்விடத்தே, உறுப்பில் குறைவுபடாத உயர் பிறப்பாகிய இம்மனிதப் பிறப்பில் என்னைப் பிறப்பித்தருளிய தேவரீரது பேரருட் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை என்னென்று கருதி என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
translit: cutta caṉmārkka lakṣiya cattiya ñāṉak kaṭavuḷē! jīvarkaḷāṟ kaṇittaṟiyappaṭāta periya ulakiṉkaṇṇē, pērācai peruṅkōpam perumōkam perumatam perulōpam pēraḻukkāṟu pērakaṅkāram peruvayiram perumaṭam perumayakkam mutaliya peruṅkuṟṟaṅkaḷē perumpālum viḷaivataṟkurimaiyākiya maṟṟai iṭaṅkaḷiṟ piṟappiyāmal, kuṇaṅkaḷē perumpālum viḷaitaṟkuriya ivviṭattē, uṟuppil kuṟaivupaṭāta uyar piṟappākiya immaṉitap piṟappil eṉṉaip piṟappittaruḷiya tēvarīratu pēraruṭ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai eṉṉeṉṟu karuti eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
translation: O God of true wisdom, the goal of Suddha Sanmarkkam! In this great world, which living beings cannot measure, there are other places where great faults mostly grow: great greed, great anger, great lust, great pride, great miserliness, great envy, great egotism, great hatred, great folly, great delusion and the rest. You did not have me born in those places. Here, where good qualities mostly grow, You graciously had me born in this human birth, the high birth, lacking in no limb. How shall I contemplate the power of the great compassion of Your great grace! How shall I praise it!
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as the God of true wisdom (cattiya ñāṉam) who is the goal (lakṣiyam) of Suddha Sanmarkkam. Then he gives thanks for where and how he was born. The world, he says, is so great that living beings cannot measure it. In other places in it, great faults mostly grow, and he names ten, each one called great: greed, anger, lust, pride, miserliness, envy, egotism, hatred, folly and delusion. God did not have him born there. He was born "here" (ivviṭattē), where good qualities mostly grow, and in the human birth, which he calls the high birth, lacking in no limb. A footnote in the Urainadai editions describes this passage as his thanks to God for having him born in the Tamil land; in section 21 he gives thanks that God fixed his mind on Tamil. In section 2 he called the human body the highest of all the bodies that are born, with six kinds of awareness; here he adds the place and the whole body. All of it, he says, is the work of the great compassion of God's great grace, and he can only ask how he shall contemplate it and how he shall praise it.

sections.title: Protected from Infancy to Boyhood

tamil: அருட்பெரு வெளியின்கண்ணே அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி வடிவராகி விகற்பமில்லாது விளங்குகின்ற மெய்ப்பொருட் கடவுளே! சிசுப் பருவந் தொடங்கிக் குமாரப் பருவம் வரையில் பேய்வெருட்டல் தோஷந்தாங்கல் பால் எதிரெடுத்தல் சவலைக்குருந்தாதல் நோய்ப் பிணிப்புண்டல் பசியால் அரற்றல் பயத்தால் உலம்புதல் உண்டி உவட்டல் உடம்பொடுநேர்தல் முதலிய எவ்வகைத் தடைகளாலும் தடைபடாமல் எனது அகத்தும் புறத்தும் காத்திருந்து வளர்த்தருளிய தேவரீரது பேரருட் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை என்னென்று கருதி என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
translit: aruṭperu veḷiyiṉkaṇṇē aruṭperuñjōti vaṭivarāki vikaṟpamillātu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa meypporuṭ kaṭavuḷē! cicup paruvan toṭaṅkik kumārap paruvam varaiyil pēyveruṭṭal tōṣantāṅkal pāl etireṭuttal cavalaikkuruntātal nōyp piṇippuṇṭal paciyāl araṟṟal payattāl ulamputal uṇṭi uvaṭṭal uṭampoṭunērtal mutaliya evvakait taṭaikaḷālum taṭaipaṭāmal eṉatu akattum puṟattum kāttiruntu vaḷarttaruḷiya tēvarīratu pēraruṭ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai eṉṉeṉṟu karuti eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
translation: O God, the True Reality, who shines without any division in the form of Arut Perum Jothi in the great Space of Grace! From infancy until boyhood You kept watch within me and without and raised me, so that no hindrance of any kind hindered me: being frightened by spirits, suffering affliction, vomiting milk, becoming a weakly child, being seized by disease, crying from hunger, crying out in fear, turning from food, mishaps to the body and the rest. How shall I contemplate the power of the great compassion of Your great grace! How shall I praise it!
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as the True Reality (meypporuḷ), who shines without any division in the form of Arut Perum Jothi in the great Space of Grace (aruṭperu veḷi). Then he looks back on his childhood, from infancy (cicup paruvam) to boyhood (kumārap paruvam), and names its dangers one by one: being frightened by spirits, suffering affliction (tōṣam), bringing up milk, becoming a weakly child (cavalai), being seized by disease, crying from hunger, crying out in fear, turning from food, and mishaps to the body. None of them hindered him, because God kept watch within him and without and raised him. The God who shines in the great Space of Grace is the same God who guarded a small child from hunger and fright. The next two sections stay in his boyhood: the faults God kept him from and the good ways God led him into (section 19), and the learning God gave him from within (section 20).

sections.title: Kept from Childish Faults, Led to Good Ways

tamil: அறிவார் அறியும் வண்ணங்களெல்லாம் உடைய பேரருட் பெருஞ்ஜோதிப் பெருந்தகைக் கடவுளே! குமாரப் பருவத்திற்றானே உலகில் சிறுவர்களுடன் கூடிச் சிறுவிளையாட்டியற்றல் சிற்றுண்டிவிழைதல் சித்திரம்பயிறல் அதிசயம்பார்த்தல் அசங்கியம் பேசல் அவலித்தழுதல் சிறுசண்டை செய்தல் சிறுகுறும்பியற்றல் தன்வசத்துழலல் தாய்வயிற் சலித்தல் முதலிய குற்றங்களில் என்னைச் சிறிதும் செலுத்தாமல் ஓர் சிறிது அறிவு விளங்கப் புரிந்து இடந்தனித்திருத்தல் இச்சையின்றி நுகர்தல் ஜெபதபஞ்செய்தல் தெய்வம்பராவல் பிறவுயிர்க்கிரங்கல் பெருங்குணம்பற்றல் பாடிப்பணிதல் பத்திசெய்திருத்தல் முதலிய நற்செய்கைகளில் என்னைச் செலுத்திய தேவரீரது பேரருட் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை என்னென்று கருதி என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
translit: aṟivār aṟiyum vaṇṇaṅkaḷellām uṭaiya pēraruṭ peruñjōtip peruntakaik kaṭavuḷē! kumārap paruvattiṟṟāṉē ulakil ciṟuvarkaḷuṭaṉ kūṭic ciṟuviḷaiyāṭṭiyaṟṟal ciṟṟuṇṭiviḻaital cittirampayiṟal aticayampārttal acaṅkiyam pēcal avalittaḻutal ciṟucaṇṭai ceytal ciṟukuṟumpiyaṟṟal taṉvacattuḻalal tāyvayiṟ calittal mutaliya kuṟṟaṅkaḷil eṉṉaic ciṟitum celuttāmal ōr ciṟitu aṟivu viḷaṅkap purintu iṭantaṉittiruttal iccaiyiṉṟi nukartal jepatapañceytal teyvamparāval piṟavuyirkkiraṅkal peruṅkuṇampaṟṟal pāṭippaṇital patticeytiruttal mutaliya naṟceykaikaḷil eṉṉaic celuttiya tēvarīratu pēraruṭ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai eṉṉeṉṟu karuti eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
translation: O God of great nobility, Arut Perum Jothi of great grace, who has every form that knowers know! In my boyhood itself, You did not lead me even a little into faults such as joining the boys of the world in childish games, craving snacks, practising idle arts, gaping at spectacles, speaking foul words, whining and wailing, picking petty quarrels, doing small mischief, roaming at my own will and fretting at my mother. You made a little understanding shine in me and led me into good deeds such as staying alone in a secluded place, eating without craving, doing prayer and austerity, praising God, having compassion for other living beings, holding to noble qualities, singing and bowing down, and abiding in devotion. How shall I contemplate the power of the great compassion of Your great grace! How shall I praise it!
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as the God of great nobility, Arut Perum Jothi of great grace, who has every form that knowers know. Then he tells what God did in his boyhood (kumārap paruvam). God did not lead him, even a little, into the faults of boys: childish games, craving snacks, idle arts, gaping at spectacles, foul talk, whining, petty quarrels, mischief, roaming at his own will, fretting at his mother. God made a little understanding shine in him and led him into good deeds: staying alone, eating without craving, prayer and austerity (japa and tapas), praising God, having compassion for other living beings (piṟavuyirkku iraṅkal), holding to noble qualities, singing and bowing, abiding in devotion. Compassion for other lives already stands among a child's good deeds; in section 25 it returns as the good endeavour of compassion that longs for all living beings to attain bliss. He claims none of these virtues as his own. The verbs belong to God: You did not lead me into faults; You led me into good deeds. So the section ends in the petition's refrain.

sections.title: The Inner Teacher

tamil: எல்லாம் ஆனவராயும் ஒன்றும் அல்லாதவராயும் எல்லா அண்ட சராசரங்களின் அகத்தும் புறத்தும் நிறைந்து விளங்குகின்ற தனித்தலைமைக் கடவுளே! குமாரப் பருவத்தில் என்னைக் கல்வியில் பயிற்றும் ஆசிரியரையின்றியே என் தரத்தில் பயின்று அறிதற்கருமையாகிய கல்விப் பயிற்சியை எனதுள்ளகத்தே இருந்து பயிற்றுவித்தருளினீர்.
translit: ellām āṉavarāyum oṉṟum allātavarāyum ellā aṇṭa carācaraṅkaḷiṉ akattum puṟattum niṟaintu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa taṉittalaimaik kaṭavuḷē! kumārap paruvattil eṉṉaik kalviyil payiṟṟum āciriyaraiyiṉṟiyē eṉ tarattil payiṉṟu aṟitaṟkarumaiyākiya kalvip payiṟciyai eṉatuḷḷakattē iruntu payiṟṟuvittaruḷiṉīr.
translation: O God of unique supremacy, who is all things and yet none of them, and who fills and shines within and without all the universes and all that moves and does not move! In my boyhood, with no teacher to train me in learning, You dwelt within my heart and graciously trained me in a learning that, at my level, was very hard to study and to know.
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as the God of unique supremacy, who is all things and yet none of them, and who fills and shines within and without all the universes and all that moves and does not move. That same God dwelt within one boy's heart. In his boyhood no teacher trained him in learning (kalvi). God trained him from within his heart (uḷḷakam), in a learning that at his level was very hard to study and to know. A footnote in the Urainadai editions takes this passage as his own testimony that God taught him and that he studied under no other teacher. He claims no credit for it. As in every stage this petition tells, the doer is God: You trained me. The next section says where that inner training led: to Tamil, and to the hymns God made him sing in it.

sections.title: Tamil, the Southern Language Given by Grace

tamil: இடம்பத்தையும் ஆரவாரத்தையும் பிரயாசத்தையும் பெருமறைப்பையும் போதுபோக்கையும் உண்டுபண்ணுகின்ற ஆரிய முதலிய பாஷைகளில் எனக்கு ஆசை செல்லவொட்டாது, பயிலுதற்கும் அறிதற்கும் மிகவும் இலேசுடையதாய்ப் பாடுதற்கும் துதித்தற்கும் மிகவும் இனிமை உடையதாய் சாகாக்கல்வியை இலேசில் அறிவிப்பதாய்த் திருவருள் வலத்தாற் கிடைத்த தென்மொழி ஒன்றனிடத்தே மனம் பற்றச்செய்து அத்தென்மொழிகளால் பல்வகைத் தோத்திரப் பாட்டுக்களைப் பாடுவித்தருளினீர்.
translit: iṭampattaiyum āravārattaiyum pirayācattaiyum perumaṟaippaiyum pōtupōkkaiyum uṇṭupaṇṇukiṉṟa āriya mutaliya pāṣaikaḷil eṉakku ācai cellavoṭṭātu, payilutaṟkum aṟitaṟkum mikavum ilēcuṭaiyatāyp pāṭutaṟkum tutittaṟkum mikavum iṉimai uṭaiyatāy cākākkalviyai ilēcil aṟivippatāyt tiruvaruḷ valattāṟ kiṭaitta teṉmoḻi oṉṟaṉiṭattē maṉam paṟṟacceytu atteṉmoḻikaḷāl palvakait tōttirap pāṭṭukkaḷaip pāṭuvittaruḷiṉīr.
translation: You did not let my desire go toward Sanskrit and the other such languages, which breed pomp, clamour, toil, great concealment and the wasting of time. You made my mind hold to one language alone, the southern language, which came to me by the strength of Your holy grace: it is very easy to learn and to know, very sweet to sing and to praise in, and it makes known with ease the learning of deathlessness. In that southern tongue You graciously made me sing hymns of praise of many kinds.
commentary: Vallalar names five things that Āriyam (Sanskrit) and the other such languages produce: pomp (iṭampam), clamour (āravāram), toil (pirayācam), great concealment (perumaṟaippu) and the wasting of time (pōtupōkku). God did not let his desire go toward them. God made his mind hold to the southern language alone, Tamil (teṉmoḻi), which came to him by the strength of God's holy grace (tiruvaruḷ valam). He gives Tamil three marks. It is very easy to learn and to know. It is very sweet to sing and to praise in. It makes known with ease the learning of deathlessness (cākākkalvi). In that language God made him sing hymns of praise of many kinds, the songs later gathered as Thiru Arutpa. Here too the choice is God's: God turned his desire away, and God made his mind hold.

sections.title: Caste and Life-stage Customs Made Known as False

tamil: அச்சிறு பருவத்திற்றானே ஜாதிஆசாரம் ஆசிரமஆசாரம் என்னும் பொய்யுலக ஆசாரத்தைப் பொய்யென்றறிவித்து அவைகளை அனுட்டியாமல் தடை செய்வித்து அப்பருவம் ஏறுந்தோறும் ஏறுந்தோறும் எனது அறிவை விளக்கஞ் செய்து செய்து என்னை மேல்நிலையில் ஏற்றி ஏற்றி நிலைக்கவைத் தருளினீர்.
translit: acciṟu paruvattiṟṟāṉē jāti-ācāram ācirama-ācāram eṉṉum poyyulaka ācārattaip poyyeṉṟaṟivittu avaikaḷai aṉuṭṭiyāmal taṭai ceyvittu apparuvam ēṟuntōṟum ēṟuntōṟum eṉatu aṟivai viḷakkañ ceytu ceytu eṉṉai mēlnilaiyil ēṟṟi ēṟṟi nilaikkavait taruḷiṉīr.
translation: At that same young age, You made me know that the false worldly custom called caste custom and life-stage custom is false, and You kept me from practising them. And as that age advanced, step after step, You made my understanding shine again and again, raised me again and again to a higher state, and graciously set me firm there.
commentary: At that same young age God made Vallalar know that caste custom (jāti ācāram) and the custom of the stages of life (ācirama ācāram) are false worldly custom (poyyulaka ācāram). He says "false" twice in one breath: false worldly custom, made known as false. God did more than make him know; God kept him from practising them. Vallalar holds this verdict throughout his teaching. In the Small True Petition he prays that the worldly customs, notions and distinctions such as varna and ashrama never take hold of the minds of those who pray. In the Arut Perum Jothi Agaval he praises the Light who made him know at the very beginning that caste, sect and religion are false. Then, as his age advanced step after step (ēṟuntōṟum ēṟuntōṟum), God made his understanding shine again and again, raised him again and again to a higher state, and set him firm there. The doubled words (ceytu ceytu, ēṟṟi ēṟṟi) show the work done over and over, and every step is God's.

sections.title: Suppressing Youthful Desires

tamil: வாலிபப் பருவம் அடுக்குந் தருணத்திற்றானே அப்பருவத்திற்கு மிகவும் உரிய விடய இச்சைகளைச் சிறிதும் தலையெடுக்க வொட்டாது அடக்குவித்தருளினீர்.
translit: vālipap paruvam aṭukkun taruṇattiṟṟāṉē apparuvattiṟku mikavum uriya viṭaya iccaikaḷaic ciṟitum talaiyeṭukka voṭṭātu aṭakkuvittaruḷiṉīr.
translation: At the very time youth was drawing near, You graciously held down the desires for sense objects that belong most of all to that age, and did not let them raise their head even a little.
commentary: At the very time youth (vālipap paruvam) was drawing near, God held down the desires for sense objects (viṭaya iccai) that belong most of all to that age, and did not let them raise their head even a little. Youth is a new stage; until now the petition has spoken of boyhood (kumārap paruvam). Vallalar does not say he conquered these desires by effort. He says God subdued them. A footnote in the Urainadai editions takes this passage as his own testimony that he had no desires for sense objects in his youth. It also prepares what comes later. In section 25 God does not let his understanding cling, even by an atom's measure, to the desires for gold, women and land. There, freedom from desire comes joined to the compassion that longs for all living beings to attain bliss.

sections.title: One True God; Kept from Religions, Sects and Paths

tamil: அவ்வாலிபப் பருவம் தோன்றுதற்கு முன்னரே எல்லா உயிர்கட்கும் இன்பந் தருவதற்கு அகத்தும் புறத்தும் விளங்குகின்ற அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி உண்மைக் கடவுள் ஒருவரே உள்ளார் என்று அறிகின்ற மெய்யறிவை விளக்குவித்தருளினீர். வாலிபப்பருவம் தோன்றிய போதே சைவம் வைணவம் சமணம் பவுத்தம் முதலாகப் பலபெயர் கொண்டு பலபட விரிந்த அளவிறந்த சமயங்களும் அச்சமயங்களில் குறித்த சாதனங்களும் தெய்வங்களும் கதிகளும் தத்துவ சித்தி விகற்பங்கள் என்றும், அவ்வச் சமயங்களில் பலபட விரிந்த வேதங்கள் ஆகமங்கள் புராணங்கள் சாத்திரங்கள் முதலிய கலைகள் எல்லாம் தத்துவ சித்திக் கற்பனைக் கலைகள் என்றும், உள்ளபடியே எனக்கு அறிவித்து அச்சமயாசாரங்களைச் சிறிதும் அனுட்டியாமல் தடைசெய்வித் தருளினீர். அன்றியும் வேதாந்தம் சித்தாந்தம் போதாந்தம் நாதாந்தம் யோகாந்தம் கலாந்தம் முதலாகப் பலபெயர் கொண்டு பலபட விரிந்த மதங்களும் மார்க்கங்களும் சுத்த சன்மார்க்க அனுபவ லேச சித்தி பேதங்கள் என்று அறிவித்து அவைகளையும் அனுட்டியாதபடி தடைசெய்வித் தருளினீர்.
translit: avvālipap paruvam tōṉṟutaṟku muṉṉarē ellā uyirkaṭkum iṉpan taruvataṟku akattum puṟattum viḷaṅkukiṉṟa aruṭperuñjōti uṇmaik kaṭavuḷ oruvarē uḷḷār eṉṟu aṟikiṉṟa meyyaṟivai viḷakkuvittaruḷiṉīr. vālipapparuvam tōṉṟiya pōtē caivam vaiṇavam camaṇam pavuttam mutalākap palapeyar koṇṭu palapaṭa virinta aḷaviṟanta camayaṅkaḷum accamayaṅkaḷil kuṟitta cātaṉaṅkaḷum teyvaṅkaḷum katikaḷum tattuva citti vikaṟpaṅkaḷ eṉṟum, avvac camayaṅkaḷil palapaṭa virinta vētaṅkaḷ ākamaṅkaḷ purāṇaṅkaḷ cāttiraṅkaḷ mutaliya kalaikaḷ ellām tattuva cittik kaṟpaṉaik kalaikaḷ eṉṟum, uḷḷapaṭiyē eṉakku aṟivittu accamayācāraṅkaḷaic ciṟitum aṉuṭṭiyāmal taṭaiceyvit taruḷiṉīr. aṉṟiyum vētāntam cittāntam pōtāntam nātāntam yōkāntam kalāntam mutalākap palapeyar koṇṭu palapaṭa virinta mataṅkaḷum mārkkaṅkaḷum cutta caṉmārkka aṉupava lēca citti pētaṅkaḷ eṉṟu aṟivittu avaikaḷaiyum aṉuṭṭiyātapaṭi taṭaiceyvit taruḷiṉīr.
translation: Even before that youth appeared, You graciously made shine in me the true knowledge that knows there is only one true God, Arut Perum Jothi, who shines within and without to give bliss to all living beings. As soon as youth appeared, You made me know, exactly as they are, that the countless religions, Saivism, Vaishnavism, Jainism, Buddhism and the rest, which bear many names and spread out in many ways, together with the practices, gods and goals laid down in those religions, are varieties of attainment within the tattvas; and that all the lore spread out in many ways in each of those religions, the Vedas, Agamas, Puranas, Sastras and the rest, is imagined lore of attainment within the tattvas. And You graciously kept me from practising the customs of those religions even a little. Moreover, You made me know that the sects and paths, Vedanta, Siddhanta, Bodhanta, Nadanta, Yoganta, Kalanta and the rest, which bear many names and spread out in many ways, are distinctions of attainment of a slight fraction of the Suddha Sanmarkkam experience; and You graciously kept me from practising them too.
commentary: Even before his youth began, God made the true knowledge shine in Vallalar: there is only one true God, Arut Perum Jothi, who shines within and without to give bliss to all living beings. Then, as youth appeared, God made known to him, "exactly as they are" (uḷḷapaṭiyē), what the religions and their scriptures are. First, the countless religions, Saivism, Vaishnavism, Jainism, Buddhism and the rest, with the practices, gods and goals laid down in them, are varieties of attainment within the tattvas (tattuva citti vikaṟpaṅkaḷ). The tattvas are the constituent principles of which bodies, minds and worlds are made. Second, all their scriptures, the Vedas, Agamas, Puranas, Sastras and the rest, are imagined lore of attainment within the tattvas (tattuva cittik kaṟpaṉaik kalaikaḷ). God kept him from practising the customs of those religions even a little. Third, the sects and paths (mataṅkaḷ, mārkkaṅkaḷ) named Vedanta, Siddhanta, Bodhanta, Nadanta, Yoganta, Kalanta and the rest are distinctions of attainment of a slight fraction (lēcam) of the Suddha Sanmarkkam experience. God kept him from practising these too. The grading is his own: the religions and their scriptures he places within the tattvas; the sects and paths he measures against the Suddha Sanmarkkam experience, as a slight fraction of it. The knowledge of the one true God came first, and the verdicts followed. In the Small True Petition the same religions, sects and paths are named the chief obstacle to Suddha Sanmarkkam.

sections.title: Compassion for All Life and the Great Life of Bliss

tamil: அங்ஙனம் செய்வித்ததுமன்றி, உலகியற்கண் பொன்விஷய இச்சை பெண்விஷய இச்சை மண்விஷய இச்சை முதலிய எவ்விஷய இச்சைகளிலும் என் அறிவை ஓரணுத்துணையும் பற்றுவிக்காமல் எல்லா உயிர்களையும் பொதுமையில் நோக்கி எல்லா உயிர்களும் இன்பமடைதல் வேண்டுமென்னும் கருணை நன்முயற்சியைப் பெறுவித்துச் சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத் தனிநெறி ஒன்றையே பற்றுவித்து எக்காலத்தும் நாசமடையாத சுத்ததேகம் பிரணவதேகம் ஞானதேகம் என்னும் சாகாக் கலானுபவ தேகங்களும், தன் சுதந்தரத்தால் தத்துவங்கள் எல்லாவற்றையும் நடத்துகின்ற தனிப்பெரு வல்லபமும் கடவுள் ஒருவரே என்று அறிகின்ற உண்மை ஞானமும் கருமசித்தி யோகசித்தி ஞானசித்தி முதலிய எல்லாச் சித்திகளும் பெறுகின்ற அருட்பேறும் பெற்று வாழ்கின்ற பேரின்பப் பெருவாழ்வில் என்னை அடைவிப்பதற்குத் திருவுளங்கொண்டு அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதியராகி நான் எவ்விதத்தும் அறிதற்கரிய உண்மைப் பேரறிவை அறிவித்தும், நான் எவ்விதத்தும் காண்பதற்கரிய உண்மைப் பெருங் காட்சிகளைக் காட்டுவித்தும், நான் எவ்விதத்தும் செய்தற்கரிய உண்மைப் பெருஞ் செயல்களைச் செய்வித்தும், நான் எவ்விதத்தும் அடைதற்கரிய உண்மைப் பெரு நன்மைகளை அடைவித்தும், நான் எவ்விதத்தும் அனுபவித்தற்கரிய உண்மைப் பேரனுபவங்களை அனுபவிப்பித்தும் எனது அகத்தினும் புறத்தினும் இடைவிடாது காத்தருளி எனது உள்ளகத்திருந்து உயிரிற்கலந்து பெருந்தயவால் திருநடஞ்செய்தருளுகின்றீர். இங்ஙனஞ் செய்தருள்கின்ற தேவரீரது திருவருட் பெருங்கருணைத் திறத்தை என்னென்று கருதி என்னென்று துதிப்பேன்!
திருச்சிற்றம்பலம்
translit: aṅṅaṉam ceyvittatumaṉṟi, ulakiyaṟkaṇ poṉviṣaya iccai peṇviṣaya iccai maṇviṣaya iccai mutaliya evviṣaya iccaikaḷilum eṉ aṟivai ōraṇuttuṇaiyum paṟṟuvikkāmal ellā uyirkaḷaiyum potumaiyil nōkki ellā uyirkaḷum iṉpamaṭaital vēṇṭumeṉṉum karuṇai naṉmuyaṟciyaip peṟuvittuc cutta caṉmārkkat taṉineṟi oṉṟaiyē paṟṟuvittu ekkālattum nācamaṭaiyāta cuttatēkam piraṇavatēkam ñāṉatēkam eṉṉum cākāk kalāṉupava tēkaṅkaḷum, taṉ cutantarattāl tattuvaṅkaḷ ellāvaṟṟaiyum naṭattukiṉṟa taṉipperu vallapamum kaṭavuḷ oruvarē eṉṟu aṟikiṉṟa uṇmai ñāṉamum karumacitti yōkacitti ñāṉacitti mutaliya ellāc cittikaḷum peṟukiṉṟa aruṭpēṟum peṟṟu vāḻkiṉṟa pēriṉpap peruvāḻvil eṉṉai aṭaivippataṟkut tiruvuḷaṅkoṇṭu aruṭperuñjōtiyarāki nāṉ evvitattum aṟitaṟkariya uṇmaip pēraṟivai aṟivittum, nāṉ evvitattum kāṇpataṟkariya uṇmaip peruṅ kāṭcikaḷaik kāṭṭuvittum, nāṉ evvitattum ceytaṟkariya uṇmaip peruñ ceyalkaḷaic ceyvittum, nāṉ evvitattum aṭaitaṟkariya uṇmaip peru naṉmaikaḷai aṭaivittum, nāṉ evvitattum aṉupavittaṟkariya uṇmaip pēraṉupavaṅkaḷai aṉupavippittum eṉatu akattiṉum puṟattiṉum iṭaiviṭātu kāttaruḷi eṉatu uḷḷakattiruntu uyiriṟkalantu peruntayavāl tirunaṭañceytaruḷukiṉṟīr. iṅṅaṉañ ceytaruḷkiṉṟa tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattai eṉṉeṉṟu karuti eṉṉeṉṟu tutippēṉ!
tirucciṟṟampalam
translation: Not only did You do this. In worldly life You did not let my understanding cling, even by an atom's measure, to any desire for sense objects: the desire for gold, the desire for women, the desire for land, or any other. You gave me the good endeavour of compassion, which looks on all living beings alike and longs for all living beings to attain bliss. You made me hold to the one unique path of Suddha Sanmarkkam alone. There is a great life of supreme bliss, lived in possession of these: the bodies of the experience of the deathless art, which never perish at any time, called the pure body, the body of the primal sound Om and the body of wisdom; the unique great power that, by one's own freedom, directs all the tattvas; the true wisdom that knows there is only one God; and the gift of grace by which all attainments are obtained, the attainment of action, the attainment of yoga, the attainment of wisdom and the rest. Resolving in Your holy heart to bring me into that great life of bliss, You, as Arut Perum Jothi, made me know great true knowledge that I could in no way know. You showed me great true visions that I could in no way see. You made me do great true deeds that I could in no way do. You made me attain great true goods that I could in no way attain. You made me experience great true experiences that I could in no way experience. Guarding me without ceasing within and without, You dwell in my inmost heart, mingle with my life, and in Your great kindness You graciously perform the holy dance. How shall I contemplate the power of the great compassion of Your grace, You who graciously do all this! How shall I praise it! Tiruchitrambalam.
commentary: In the Tamil, all of this section before the refrain is a single sentence. God did more than keep Vallalar from the religions, sects and paths. In worldly life God did not let his understanding cling, even by an atom's measure, to the desire for gold, for women, for land or for any other sense object. In their place God gave him "the good endeavour of compassion" (karuṇai naṉmuyaṟci), which looks on all living beings alike (potumaiyil nōkki) and longs for all of them to attain bliss, the bliss Arut Perum Jothi shines to give them (section 24). This is Jeevakarunyam, compassion for all living beings, and in the sentence it comes before the path: then God made him hold to the one unique path of Suddha Sanmarkkam alone. Then he names the great life of supreme bliss (pēriṉpap peruvāḻvu), lived in possession of four things: the deathless bodies, Suddha Deham, Pranava Deham and Jnana Deham; the unique great power that directs all the tattvas; the true wisdom that knows there is only one God; and the gift of grace (aruṭpēṟu) by which every attainment is obtained. To bring him into that life, God, as Arut Perum Jothi, did five things beyond his reach in any way: made him know great true knowledge, showed him great true visions, made him do great true deeds, made him attain great true goods, and made him experience great true experiences. Then the verbs turn to the present. God guards him without ceasing, dwells in his inmost heart, mingles with his life, and in great kindness (peruntayavu) performs the holy dance. The closing question, asked since section 2, is in the present too: "You who graciously do all this." In the edition based on his manuscript, the petition closes, as it opened, with Tiruchitrambalam.

works.title: The True Petition of Wisdom of the Universal Pure True Path
works.translit: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Gnana Vinnappam
works.tamil: சமரச சுத்த சன்மார்க்க சத்திய ஞான விண்ணப்பம்

sections.title: The True Petition of Wisdom of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam

tamil: 3. சமரச சுத்த சன்மார்க்க சத்திய ஞான விண்ணப்பம்
திருச்சிற்றம்பலம்
translit: 3. camaraca cutta caṉmārkka cattiya ñāṉa viṇṇappam
tirucciṟṟampalam
translation: The True Petition of Wisdom of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam. Tiruchitrambalam.
commentary: The title names this work a viṇṇappam, a petition laid before God, and calls it true (cattiya) and of wisdom (ñāṉa). It also names the path in which the petition is made: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, the Universal Pure True Path. In the collected prose writings it stands third of Vallalar's four petitions, and it is often called simply the Petition of Wisdom (ñāṉa viṇṇappam). Below the title stands the sacred word Tiruchitrambalam, "the holy small hall", the name of the hall of the sacred dance at Chidambaram. The Small and the Great True Petitions also open with it, and this petition closes with it too. The printed text rests on six handwritten copies made by Vallalar's devotees. One heads it "the special petition on the holy presence of Grace" (tiruvaruṭ camuka vicēṣa viṇṇappam). Another says what it tells of: how rare is the sacred form of the holy presence of Grace, and how very rare is the power of attainment of the true sages who reached that presence. Like the Great True Petition, it speaks as "I", and it addresses God as Tēvarīr, the most reverent word for "You". Three acts run through it: to know (aṟital), to contemplate (karututal) and to praise (tutittal). In the end, as far as a servant can, Vallalar has known without knowing, contemplated without contemplating and praised without praising.

sections.title: How Shall I Begin to Know?

tamil: இயற்கை விளக்கம் என்கின்ற சத்திய ஞானசபைக் கண்ணே, இயற்கை உண்மை என்கின்ற சத்தியத் திருவுருவினராய், இயற்கை இன்பம் என்கின்ற சத்தியத் திருநடஞ் செய்தருள்கின்ற இயற்கைத் தனிப்பெருங்கருணைத் தனிப்பெரும்பதியாய தனித் தலைமைக் கடவுளே!

தேவரீர் திருவருட் சமுகத்தை அடைந்த உண்மை ஞானிகளின் சித்தி வல்லப தரத்தை வகுத்தறிந்து வாழ்த்துதும் என்று அளவிகந்த முகங்களைக் கொண்டு அளவு கடந்த நெடுங்காலம் தத்தம் அளவைகளால் தனித்தனி அளந்தளந்தும் ஒருமித்து அளந்தளந்தும் ஒருவாற்றினும் முடிவு தோற்றாமையின் வேதாகமங்கள் அனைத்தும் ஆங்காங்கு கோடித்து அதிசயிக்கின்றன என்றும், அண்ட சராசரங்கள் எல்லாவற்றையும் படைத்தல் காத்தல் துரிசு நீக்கல் முதலிய தொழில்களால் நிகழ்த்துகின்ற அதிகாரத் தலைவர்களும் எவ்வகைத் தத்துவங்களையும் காரண காரிய திறத்தால் நடத்துகின்ற சத்தி சத்தர்களும் உணர்ந்துணர்ந்தும் உணர்ச்சி செல்லாமையின் முயற்சி பற்றாது மயங்குகின்றன ரென்றும், பேரறிவாற் சிறந்த பெரியர்களெல்லாம் வியந்து வியந்து விளம்புகின்றனர். அதனால் திருவருட் சமுகத்தை யடைந்த உண்மை ஞானிகளின் சித்தி வல்லப தரத்தை ஒருவராலும் ஒருவாற்றானும் உணர்ந்து கொள்ளுதல் கூடா வென்று ஐயுறவின்றி அறிந்து கொண்டேன். இங்ஙனம் அறிந்துகொண்ட சிறியேன் அவ்வுண்மை ஞானிகளுக்குச் சித்தி வல்லப தரத்தைக் கொடுத்தருளிய திருவருட் சமுகத்தின் இயற்கை உண்மை விளக்கத் தரத்தை எங்ஙனம் அறியத் தொடங்குவேன்!
translit: iyaṟkai viḷakkam eṉkiṉṟa cattiya ñāṉacapaik kaṇṇē, iyaṟkai uṇmai eṉkiṉṟa cattiyat tiruvuruviṉarāy, iyaṟkai iṉpam eṉkiṉṟa cattiyat tirunaṭañ ceytaruḷkiṉṟa iyaṟkait taṉipperuṅkaruṇait taṉipperumpatiyāya taṉit talaimaik kaṭavuḷē!

tēvarīr tiruvaruṭ camukattai aṭainta uṇmai ñāṉikaḷiṉ citti vallapa tarattai vakuttaṟintu vāḻttutum eṉṟu aḷavikanta mukaṅkaḷaik koṇṭu aḷavu kaṭanta neṭuṅkālam tattam aḷavaikaḷāl taṉittaṉi aḷantaḷantum orumittu aḷantaḷantum oruvāṟṟiṉum muṭivu tōṟṟāmaiyiṉ vētākamaṅkaḷ aṉaittum āṅkāṅku kōṭittu aticayikkiṉṟaṉa eṉṟum, aṇṭa carācaraṅkaḷ ellāvaṟṟaiyum paṭaittal kāttal turicu nīkkal mutaliya toḻilkaḷāl nikaḻttukiṉṟa atikārat talaivarkaḷum evvakait tattuvaṅkaḷaiyum kāraṇa kāriya tiṟattāl naṭattukiṉṟa catti cattarkaḷum uṇarntuṇarntum uṇarcci cellāmaiyiṉ muyaṟci paṟṟātu mayaṅkukiṉṟaṉa reṉṟum, pēraṟivāṟ ciṟanta periyarkaḷellām viyantu viyantu viḷampukiṉṟaṉar. ataṉāl tiruvaruṭ camukattai yaṭainta uṇmai ñāṉikaḷiṉ citti vallapa tarattai oruvarālum oruvāṟṟāṉum uṇarntu koḷḷutal kūṭā veṉṟu aiyuṟaviṉṟi aṟintu koṇṭēṉ. iṅṅaṉam aṟintukoṇṭa ciṟiyēṉ avvuṇmai ñāṉikaḷukkuc citti vallapa tarattaik koṭuttaruḷiya tiruvaruṭ camukattiṉ iyaṟkai uṇmai viḷakkat tarattai eṅṅaṉam aṟiyat toṭaṅkuvēṉ!
translation: O God of unique supremacy, the unique great Lord of natural, unique and great compassion! In the True Hall of Wisdom, which is called natural illumination, You are the One whose true holy form is called natural truth, and You graciously perform the true holy dance called natural bliss! All the great ones, excelling in great knowledge, declare, marvelling again and again, that all the Vedas and Agamas set out to know by analysis, and to praise, the measure of the power of attainment of the true sages who have reached the holy presence of Your grace. With faces beyond measure, for a time beyond measure, each by its own means of measuring, they have measured it again and again, separately and together. In no way has an end appeared to them, so here and there they embellish their words, and marvel. The great ones declare too that the ruling lords, who carry on all the universes, moving and unmoving, through such functions as creation, preservation and the removal of impurity, and the energies and their agents, who run every kind of tattva by way of cause and effect, strive again and again to perceive it; but their perception cannot reach it, their effort falls short, and they stand bewildered. So I have come to know without any doubt that no one, in any way, can grasp the measure of the power of attainment of the true sages who have reached the holy presence of Grace. Knowing this, how shall I, a small one, begin to know the measure of the natural, true illumination of the holy presence of Grace, which granted that power of attainment to those true sages!
commentary: The petition opens by calling on God through three things, each called natural (iyaṟkai) and true (cattiya). Natural illumination is the True Hall of Wisdom (cattiya ñāṉacapai). Natural truth is God's true holy form. Natural bliss is the true holy dance that God graciously performs in that Hall. Natural means God's own nature: not made, and not received from anything else. Vallalar calls Him the unique great Lord of natural, unique and great compassion, the God of unique supremacy.

Then he reports what the great ones declare, marvelling again and again. All the Vedas and Agamas set out to know and praise the power of attainment (citti vallapam) of the true sages who have reached the holy presence of God's grace (tiruvaruṭ camukam). For a time beyond measure they measured it, each by its own means and all together, found no end, and so embellished their words and marvelled. Neither the ruling lords of creation, preservation and the removal of impurity, nor the energies and their agents who run the tattvas, can reach it; they stand bewildered. So Vallalar knows without doubt that no one can grasp that power. How then shall he, a small one, begin to know the holy presence that gave it? This is the first of three questions: how shall he begin to know, to contemplate (section 3) and to praise (section 4)?

sections.title: How Shall I Begin to Contemplate?

tamil: மலத்திற் புழுத்த புழுவினுஞ் சிறியேன் பொய்யறிவாற் புனைந்து உரைத்த பொய்யுரைகளையும் மெய்யுரைகளாகக் கருணையினாற் கடைக்கணித்தருளிய அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி ஆண்டவரே! தேவரீரது திருவருட் சமுகத்தின் இயற்கைப் பெருங் கருணைப் பெருந்தன்மையைக் கருதுதற்கு விரும்பிய ஐந்தொழிற் கருத்தர் முதலியோர் தூய்மையுடைமை அன்புடைமை முதலிய சுபகுணங்களைக் கருதுதற் கருவியாய தமது கரணங்கள் முற்றப் பெற்றிலவென்று கருதுதலின்றி எண்ணி எண்ணி இரங்குகின்றனர் என்று அறிவுடையோர் வியந்துரைத்தலைப் பலகாற் பயின்று கேட்டறிந்தேன். இங்ஙனம் கேட்டறிந்த சிறியரிற் சிறியேன் அத்திருவருட் சமுகத்தின் இயற்கைப் பெருங்கருணைப் பெருந்தன்மையைக் காமம் வெகுளி முதலிய அவகுணங்கட்கெல்லாம் வைப்பிடமாகிய பராய் முருட்டன்ன கருங்கற் கரணத்தால் எங்ஙனம் கருதத் தொடங்குவேன்!
translit: malattiṟ puḻutta puḻuviṉuñ ciṟiyēṉ poyyaṟivāṟ puṉaintu uraitta poyyuraikaḷaiyum meyyuraikaḷākak karuṇaiyiṉāṟ kaṭaikkaṇittaruḷiya aruṭperuñjōti āṇṭavarē! tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭ camukattiṉ iyaṟkaip peruṅ karuṇaip peruntaṉmaiyaik karututaṟku virumpiya aintoḻiṟ karuttar mutaliyōr tūymaiyuṭaimai aṉpuṭaimai mutaliya cupakuṇaṅkaḷaik karututaṟ karuviyāya tamatu karaṇaṅkaḷ muṟṟap peṟṟilaveṉṟu karututaliṉṟi eṇṇi eṇṇi iraṅkukiṉṟaṉar eṉṟu aṟivuṭaiyōr viyanturaittalaip palakāṟ payiṉṟu kēṭṭaṟintēṉ. iṅṅaṉam kēṭṭaṟinta ciṟiyariṟ ciṟiyēṉ attiruvaruṭ camukattiṉ iyaṟkaip peruṅkaruṇaip peruntaṉmaiyaik kāmam vekuḷi mutaliya avakuṇaṅkaṭkellām vaippiṭamākiya parāy muruṭṭaṉṉa karuṅkaṟ karaṇattāl eṅṅaṉam karutat toṭaṅkuvēṉ!
translation: O Lord Arut Perum Jothi, who in Your compassion cast Your gracious glance on even the false words that I, smaller even than the worm bred in dung, made up from false knowledge and spoke, and took them as true words! The lords of the five functions and others wished to contemplate the great nature of the natural, great compassion of the holy presence of Your grace. But holding that their inner instruments, their instruments of contemplation, have not attained in full the auspicious qualities, such as purity and love, they do not contemplate it; they think on this again and again, and grieve. This I have heard and learned many times over, as the wise told of it in wonder. Having heard and learned this, how shall I, the smallest of the small, begin to contemplate the great nature of the natural, great compassion of that holy presence of Grace, with an inner instrument of black stone, like the gnarled stump of the parāy tree, the storehouse of all evil qualities, such as lust and anger!
commentary: Vallalar calls on Lord Arut Perum Jothi, the Supreme Light of Grace, who in compassion looked on his false words, made up from false knowledge, as true words. He calls himself smaller even than the worm bred in dung. Then he tells what the wise have told him many times, in wonder. The lords of the five functions and others wished to contemplate the compassion of the holy presence of God's grace. But the instruments they would contemplate with, their inner faculties (karaṇam), have not attained in full such auspicious qualities as purity and love. Knowing this, they hold back from contemplating it, think on it again and again, and grieve. The passage names what contemplating God's compassion asks of the one who contemplates: auspicious qualities such as purity (tūymaiyuṭaimai) and love (aṉpuṭaimai).

Vallalar now turns this on himself. How shall he, the smallest of the small, begin? His own inner instrument is the storehouse of every evil quality, such as lust and anger: the very opposite of the auspicious qualities the lords have not attained in full. He gives it two images of hardness: it is like the gnarled stump of the parāy tree, a hard and knotted wood, and it is black stone. He names his own mind plainly, without excuse.

sections.title: How Shall I Begin to Praise?

tamil: நாயிற் கடையேன் செய்த குற்றங்களை எல்லாம் குணங்களாகக் கொண்டு என்னுள்ளகத்தே அமர்ந்து உயிரிற் கலந்த பெருங்கருணைப் பெருமானே! தேவரீரது திருவருட்சமுகத்தின் இயற்கைப் பெருங்குணப் பெரும்புகழைத் துதித்தற்கு விரும்பிய மூர்த்திகள் முதலியோர் துதித்தற் கருவியாய தத்தஞ் செந்நா உறுப்புகள் வாய்மைகூறல் இன்சொற்புகறல் முதலிய ஒழுக்கங்களிற் சான்றில என்று துதித்தலின்றி அச்சுற்று நிற்கின்றனர் என்று அறிஞர் உண்மை வாசகத்தால் அறிந்தேன். இங்ஙனம் அறிந்த கடையேன் பொய்யுரைத்தல் பயனிலகூறல் முதலிய தீமைக்கட் பயின்று தடித்த எனது அசுத்த நாவினால் தேவரீர் திருவருட் சமுகத்தின் இயற்கைப் பெருங்குணப் பெரும்புகழை எங்ஙனம் துதிக்கத் தொடங்குவேன்!
translit: nāyiṟ kaṭaiyēṉ ceyta kuṟṟaṅkaḷai ellām kuṇaṅkaḷākak koṇṭu eṉṉuḷḷakattē amarntu uyiriṟ kalanta peruṅkaruṇaip perumāṉē! tēvarīratu tiruvaruṭcamukattiṉ iyaṟkaip peruṅkuṇap perumpukaḻait tutittaṟku virumpiya mūrttikaḷ mutaliyōr tutittaṟ karuviyāya tattañ cennā uṟuppukaḷ vāymaikūṟal iṉcoṟpukaṟal mutaliya oḻukkaṅkaḷiṟ cāṉṟila eṉṟu tutittaliṉṟi accuṟṟu niṟkiṉṟaṉar eṉṟu aṟiñar uṇmai vācakattāl aṟintēṉ. iṅṅaṉam aṟinta kaṭaiyēṉ poyyuraittal payaṉilakūṟal mutaliya tīmaikkaṭ payiṉṟu taṭitta eṉatu acutta nāviṉāl tēvarīr tiruvaruṭ camukattiṉ iyaṟkaip peruṅkuṇap perumpukaḻai eṅṅaṉam tutikkat toṭaṅkuvēṉ!
translation: O great Lord of great compassion, who took all the faults committed by me, lower than a dog, as virtues, and who sits within my heart, mingled with my soul! The deities and others wished to praise the great glory of the natural, great qualities of the holy presence of Your grace. But holding that their own fine tongues, the organs that are their instruments of praise, are not perfected in such disciplines as speaking truth and speaking sweet words, they do not praise; they stand in fear. This I have learned from the true words of the learned. Having learned this, how shall I, the lowest one, begin to praise the great glory of the natural, great qualities of the holy presence of Your grace with my impure tongue, grown thick from practice in evils such as telling lies and speaking useless words!
commentary: Calling himself lower than a dog, Vallalar calls on God as the great Lord of great compassion, who took all his faults as virtues and who sits within his heart, mingled with his very soul. Then he tells what he learned from the true words of the learned. The deities (mūrttikaḷ) and others wished to praise the great glory of the natural great qualities of the holy presence of God's grace. But they hold that their tongues, the instruments of praise, are not perfected in such disciplines (oḻukkam) as speaking truth and speaking sweetly. So they do not praise; they stand in fear. As contemplating God's compassion asks for purity and love (section 3), praising His glory asks for a tongue perfected in truth and sweet speech.

As with contemplation, Vallalar turns what he has learned onto himself. His own tongue is impure (acutta), grown thick from practice in the opposite: telling lies and speaking useless words. With such a tongue, how shall he, the lowest one (kaṭaiyēṉ), begin to praise? Like the stone-hard mind of section 3, the impure, thickened tongue is named plainly.

sections.title: The Overflowing Desire to Know, Contemplate and Praise

tamil: அண்ட பிண்ட முதலிய எல்லாவற்றிற்கும் அகத்தும் புறத்தும் நிறைந்து விளங்குகின்ற அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதித் தனிப்பெரும் பதியாய பூரணரே! தேவரீர் திருவருட் சமுகத்தின் இயற்கை உண்மைத் தரத்தை அறிதல் வேண்டு மென்றும், இயற்கைப் பெருங் கருணைப் பெருந் தன்மையைக் கருதுதல் வேண்டுமென்றும், இயற்கைப் பெருங்குணப் பெரும்புகழைத் துதித்தல் வேண்டுமென்றும், எனது உள்ளகத்தே ஓவாதுறைந்து ஊற்றெழுந்து விரைந்து விரைந்து மேன்மேற் பெருகுகின்ற பேராசைப் பெருவெள்ளம் அணைகடந்து செல்கின்றதாகலின், "அறிவார் அறிகின்ற வண்ணங்களும் கருதுவார் கருதுகின்ற வண்ணங்களும் துதிப்பார் துதிக்கின்ற வண்ணங்களும் ஆகிய எல்லா வண்ணங்களையும் உடையவர் அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதித் தனிப்பெருங்கடவுள்" என்ற சத்தியஞானிகளது உண்மை வாசகத்தைப் பற்றுக்கோடாகக் கொண்டு, தன்மைசாலாத் தமியேன் அறிதற்கும் கருதுதற்கும் துதித்தற்கும் தொடங்கினேன்.
translit: aṇṭa piṇṭa mutaliya ellāvaṟṟiṟkum akattum puṟattum niṟaintu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa aruṭperuñjōtit taṉipperum patiyāya pūraṇarē! tēvarīr tiruvaruṭ camukattiṉ iyaṟkai uṇmait tarattai aṟital vēṇṭu meṉṟum, iyaṟkaip peruṅ karuṇaip perun taṉmaiyaik karututal vēṇṭumeṉṟum, iyaṟkaip peruṅkuṇap perumpukaḻait tutittal vēṇṭumeṉṟum, eṉatu uḷḷakattē ōvātuṟaintu ūṟṟeḻuntu viraintu viraintu mēṉmēṟ perukukiṉṟa pērācaip peruveḷḷam aṇaikaṭantu celkiṉṟatākaliṉ, "aṟivār aṟikiṉṟa vaṇṇaṅkaḷum karutuvār karutukiṉṟa vaṇṇaṅkaḷum tutippār tutikkiṉṟa vaṇṇaṅkaḷum ākiya ellā vaṇṇaṅkaḷaiyum uṭaiyavar aruṭperuñjōtit taṉipperuṅkaṭavuḷ" eṉṟa cattiyañāṉikaḷatu uṇmai vācakattaip paṟṟukkōṭākak koṇṭu, taṉmaicālāt tamiyēṉ aṟitaṟkum karututaṟkum tutittaṟkum toṭaṅkiṉēṉ.
translation: O Complete One, who are Arut Perum Jothi, the unique great Lord, filling and shining within and without all things: the universe, the body and all else! A great flood of great longing dwells in my heart without ceasing; it springs up, swells faster and faster, higher and higher, and is breaking over its dam: I must know the measure of the natural truth of the holy presence of Your grace; I must contemplate the great nature of its natural, great compassion; I must praise the great glory of its natural, great qualities. So I have taken as my support the true saying of the sages of true wisdom: "Arut Perum Jothi, the unique great God, has all forms: the forms that knowers know, the forms that contemplators contemplate, and the forms that praisers praise." Holding to it, I, a lowly one without worth, have begun to know, to contemplate and to praise.
commentary: Vallalar calls on Arut Perum Jothi as the Complete One (pūraṇar), who fills and shines within and without all things: the universe (aṇṭam), the body (piṇṭam) and all else. After all he has confessed, he names his threefold longing: to know the holy presence of God's grace, to contemplate its compassion, and to praise its glory. This longing dwells in his heart without ceasing; it springs up and swells like a flood breaking over its dam. So he takes as his support (paṟṟukkōṭu) a true saying (uṇmai vācakam) of the sages of true wisdom: Arut Perum Jothi has all the forms (vaṇṇam) that knowers know, that contemplators contemplate, and that praisers praise. Holding to that word, he, who calls himself without worth, begins to know, to contemplate and to praise.

sections.title: What Are the Forms of the Holy Presence of Grace?

tamil: இங்ஙனந் தொடங்குதற்கு முன்னர், எனது அறிவிற்கும் கருத்திற்கும் நாவிற்கும் இயல்வனவாகத் தோற்றிய வண்ணங்களுள் ஒன்றேனும் ஈண்டு இயற்படத் தோற்றாமையின், அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதித் தனிப்பெருங் கடவுளே! தேவரீர் திருவருட் சமுகத்தின் இயற்கை வண்ணங்கள் எத்தன்மையவோ! எத்தன்மையவோ! என்று உணர்ந்து உணர்ந்து கருதிக்கருதி உரைத்து உரைத்து அதிசயிக்கின்றவனானேன்.
translit: iṅṅaṉan toṭaṅkutaṟku muṉṉar, eṉatu aṟiviṟkum karuttiṟkum nāviṟkum iyalvaṉavākat tōṟṟiya vaṇṇaṅkaḷuḷ oṉṟēṉum īṇṭu iyaṟpaṭat tōṟṟāmaiyiṉ, aruṭperuñjōtit taṉipperuṅ kaṭavuḷē! tēvarīr tiruvaruṭ camukattiṉ iyaṟkai vaṇṇaṅkaḷ ettaṉmaiyavō! ettaṉmaiyavō! eṉṟu uṇarntu uṇarntu karutikkaruti uraittu uraittu aticayikkiṉṟavaṉāṉēṉ.
translation: O Arut Perum Jothi, unique great God! Before I began in this way, there were forms that seemed within the reach of my knowing, my thought and my tongue; here not even one of them appears fitting. So I have become one who marvels, perceiving again and again, contemplating again and again, saying again and again: "Of what nature are the natural forms of the holy presence of Your grace! Of what nature are they!"
commentary: In the Tamil this is one sentence, with the call to God in the middle. Vallalar began on the strength of the sages' word that Arut Perum Jothi has all the forms (vaṇṇam) that knowers know, contemplators contemplate and praisers praise (section 5). Before he began, some of those forms had seemed within reach of his knowing, his thought and his tongue. Now that he stands here, not one of them appears fitting. So he marvels. Again and again he perceives, contemplates and speaks, asking: of what nature are the natural forms of the holy presence of God's grace? His knowing, his thought and his tongue are all at work, and each ends in wonder. The sentence closes: "I have become one who marvels."

sections.title: The Pure Sages Sigh: How Shall We Know?

tamil: இயற்கை உண்மைத் தனிப்பெரும் பொருளாயும் இயற்கை விளக்கத் தனிப் பெரும் பதமாயும் இயற்கை இன்பத் தனிப்பெருஞ் சுகமாயும் பிரிவின்றி நிறைந்த பெருந்தன்மையராய அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி ஆண்டவரே! தேவரீர் திருவருள் வலத்தால் பொறி புலன் கரண முதலிய தத்துவங்கள் அனைத்தையும் வென்று நின்மலராகித் தத்துவாந்தத்தில் நின்று தம் உண்மை உணர்ந்து இயற்கை உணர்ச்சியைப் பெற்று இயற்கை உண்மைக்கண் இயற்கை இன்பானுபவஞ் செய்கின்ற சுத்த யோகாந்தர்களும் சுத்த கலாந்தர்களும் சுத்த போதாந்தர்களும் சுத்த நாதாந்தர்களும் சுத்த வேதாந்தர்களும் சுத்த சித்தாந்தர்களுமாகிய சுத்த சன்மார்க்க ஞானிகளின் திருக்கூட்டங்களை நன் முயற்சியால் தனித்தனி அடைந்து பத்தியாற் பணிந்து, 'அற்புதப் பெருஞ் செயல் புரிகின்ற ஐயர்களே! அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதித் தனிப்பெரும் பதியாய கடவுளின் இயற்கைத் திருவருட் சமுகம் இருந்த வண்ணம் உள்ளம் உவந்துரைத் தருளல் வேண்டும்' என்று விண்ணப்பிக்கின்ற தோறும், 'எல்லாப் பொருள் கட்கும், எல்லாக் குணங்கட்கும் எல்லாச் செயல்கட்கும் எல்லாப் பயன்கட்கும் எல்லா அனுபவங்கட்கும் மற்றெல்லாவற்றிற்கும் உருவ சொரூப சுபாவ முதலிய இலக்கணங்கள் அனைத்தும் தாமேயாகியும் தாமல்லராகியும் தாக்கியும் தாக்கற்றும் அகத்தும் அகப்புறத்தும் புறத்தும் புறப்புறத்தும் நீக்கமின்றி நிறைந்து விளங்குகின்ற இயற்கை உண்மைக் கடவுளது இயற்கைத் திருவருட் சமுகம் இருந்த வண்ணம் அந்தோ! அந்தோ!! எங்ஙனம் அறிவோம்! எவ்வாறு கருதுவோம்! என்னென்று கூறுவோம்!' என்று அவ்வக் கூட்டங்களினுந் தனித்தனி உரைத்து உரைத்து நெகிழ்ந்து நெகிழ்ந்து நெட்டுயிர்க்கின்றார்கள் என்றும்,
translit: iyaṟkai uṇmait taṉipperum poruḷāyum iyaṟkai viḷakkat taṉip perum patamāyum iyaṟkai iṉpat taṉipperuñ cukamāyum piriviṉṟi niṟainta peruntaṉmaiyarāya aruṭperuñ jōti āṇṭavarē! tēvarīr tiruvaruḷ valattāl poṟi pulaṉ karaṇa mutaliya tattuvaṅkaḷ aṉaittaiyum veṉṟu niṉmalarākit tattuvāntattil niṉṟu tam uṇmai uṇarntu iyaṟkai uṇarcciyaip peṟṟu iyaṟkai uṇmaikkaṇ iyaṟkai iṉpāṉupavañ ceykiṉṟa cutta yōkāntarkaḷum cutta kalāntarkaḷum cutta pōtāntarkaḷum cutta nātāntarkaḷum cutta vētāntarkaḷum cutta cittāntarkaḷumākiya cutta caṉmārkka ñāṉikaḷiṉ tirukkūṭṭaṅkaḷai naṉ muyaṟciyāl taṉittaṉi aṭaintu pattiyāṟ paṇintu, 'aṟputap peruñ ceyal purikiṉṟa aiyarkaḷē! aruṭperuñ jōtit taṉipperum patiyāya kaṭavuḷiṉ iyaṟkait tiruvaruṭ camukam irunta vaṇṇam uḷḷam uvanturait taruḷal vēṇṭum' eṉṟu viṇṇappikkiṉṟa tōṟum, 'ellāp poruḷ kaṭkum, ellāk kuṇaṅkaṭkum ellāc ceyalkaṭkum ellāp payaṉkaṭkum ellā aṉupavaṅkaṭkum maṟṟellāvaṟṟiṟkum uruva corūpa cupāva mutaliya ilakkaṇaṅkaḷ aṉaittum tāmēyākiyum tāmallarākiyum tākkiyum tākkaṟṟum akattum akappuṟattum puṟattum puṟappuṟattum nīkkamiṉṟi niṟaintu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa iyaṟkai uṇmaik kaṭavuḷatu iyaṟkait tiruvaruṭ camukam irunta vaṇṇam antō! antō!! eṅṅaṉam aṟivōm! evvāṟu karutuvōm! eṉṉeṉṟu kūṟuvōm!' eṉṟu avvak kūṭṭaṅkaḷiṉun taṉittaṉi uraittu uraittu nekiḻntu nekiḻntu neṭṭuyirkkiṉṟārkaḷ eṉṟum,
translation: O Lord Arut Perum Jothi, Great One, filling all, completely and without any separation, as the unique great Reality of natural truth, the unique great State of natural illumination and the unique great Joy of natural bliss: those who have realized tell in wonder of the sages of Suddha Sanmarkkam. By the power of Your grace these sages have conquered all the tattvas, such as the sense organs, their objects and the inner faculties. They have become stainless and stand at the end of the tattvas; they have known their own truth and gained natural awareness, and in natural truth they enjoy the experience of natural bliss. They are the pure Yogantars, the pure Kalantars, the pure Bodhantars, the pure Nadantars, the pure Vedantars and the pure Siddhantars. With good effort seekers reach the holy assemblies of these sages one by one, bow before them in devotion and petition them: "O masters who perform great wonders! Be pleased, with glad hearts, to tell the natural holy presence of Grace of God, the unique great Lord Arut Perum Jothi, as it is." And every time they petition so, the sages in each of those assemblies say, one by one, again and again: "God, the natural Truth, is Himself all the marks, such as outward form, essential nature and inherent nature, of all things, all qualities, all actions, all fruits, all experiences and everything else, and He is also not them. He touches them and is untouched. He fills and shines without any gap in the inner, the inner-outer, the outer and the outer-outer. Alas! Alas!! How shall we know His natural holy presence of Grace as it is! How shall we contemplate it! What shall we say it is!" So they say, and melting, melting, they sigh deeply.
commentary: Sections 7 and 8 form one long sentence, and its frame comes only at its close: all of it is what Vallalar heard "those who have realized" (uṇarntōr) tell in wonder. It opens by calling on Lord Arut Perum Jothi, who fills all without separation as the Reality of natural truth, the State of natural illumination and the Joy of natural bliss, the three with which the petition opened (section 2). The first report concerns the sages of Suddha Sanmarkkam. By the power of God's grace they have conquered all the tattvas (the constituents of body, mind and world), have become stainless and stand where the tattvas end. They know their own truth, have gained natural awareness and enjoy natural bliss. Vallalar names them by six "ends" (antam): they are the pure Yogantars, Kalantars, Bodhantars, Nadantars, Vedantars and Siddhantars. These pure ones are themselves the sages of Suddha Sanmarkkam. The sects and paths that bear these six names he judges separately: in the Great True Petition he calls them distinctions of attainment of slight fractions of the Suddha Sanmarkkam experience. Asked to tell the natural holy presence of Grace as it is, the sages in every assembly answer alike. In their lament they speak of God: He is all the marks of all things and is also not them; He touches them and is untouched; He fills every region without a gap. Yet of His holy presence of Grace as it is, they cry: "How shall we know it! How shall we contemplate it! What shall we say it is!" Their cry echoes Vallalar's own three longings, to know, to contemplate and to praise (sections 2 to 5).

tamil: எல்லாத் தத்துவங்களையும் எல்லாத் தத்துவிகளையும் தோற்றுவித்தலும் இயக்குவித்தலும் அடக்குவித்தலும் மயக்குவித்தலும் தெளிவித்தலுமாகிய தொழில்களை எளிதிற் கொடுத்தற் குரிய பூரண சுதந்தரத்தவர்களாய், இயற்கைச் சத்தியஞான சுகானுபவ பூரண சொரூப சாத்தியர்களாய், எக்காலத்தும் எவ்விடத்தும் எவ்விதத்தும் தடைபடாத நித்திய சுத்த சத்த ஞானதேகிகளாய், பூதசித்தி, கரணசித்தி, இந்திரிய சித்தி, குண சித்தி, பிரகிருதிசித்தி, புருடசித்தி, விந்துசித்தி, பரசித்தி, சுத்தசித்தி, காலசித்தி, கலாசித்தி, விசுவசித்தி, வியோமசித்தி, பிரமசித்தி, சிவசித்தி முதலிய பிண்டசித்தி, அண்டசித்தி, பகிரண்ட சித்தி, அண்டாண்டசித்தி என்கின்ற அந்தரங்க பகிரங்க தத்துவ தத்துவி சித்திகளெல்லாவற்றையும் திருக்கடைக் கணிப்பாற் செய்யவல்லவராய், சடாந்த சமரச சத்தியராய் விளங்குகின்ற சமரச சுத்த சன்மார்க்க ஞானிகளது சித்விலாசத் திருச்சபைக் கண்ணே, புண்ணிய வசத்தால் புகுதப் பெற்று மனங்கனிந்து வணங்கி நின்று, 'சர்வ சுதந்தரராய சத்தியர்களே! இயற்கை உண்மைத் தனிப்பெரும் பதியாய கடவுளின் இயற்கைத் திருவருட் சமுகம் இருந்த வண்ணம் திருவுளம் பற்றித் திருவாய் மலர்ந்து திருவார்த்தை அளித்தருளல் வேண்டும்' என்று விண்ணப்பிக்கின்ற தோறும் திருவார்த்தை அளித்தலின்றிப் பெருங்கருணைத் திருக்கண்களில் ஆனந்தநீர் பொழிந்து சும்மா இருக்கின்றனர் என்றும், உணர்ந்தோர் வியந்துரைப்பக் கேள்வியுற்று, 'இயற்கைத் திருவருட் சமுகம் இருந்த வண்ணம் என்னையோ! என்னையோ!!' என்று குலாவிக் குலாவிக் கூவுகின்றவனானேன்.
translit: ellāt tattuvaṅkaḷaiyum ellāt tattuvikaḷaiyum tōṟṟuvittalum iyakkuvittalum aṭakkuvittalum mayakkuvittalum teḷivittalumākiya toḻilkaḷai eḷitiṟ koṭuttaṟ kuriya pūraṇa cutantarattavarkaḷāy, iyaṟkaic cattiyañāṉa cukāṉupava pūraṇa corūpa cāttiyarkaḷāy, ekkālattum evviṭattum evvitattum taṭaipaṭāta nittiya cutta catta ñāṉatēkikaḷāy, pūtacitti, karaṇacitti, intiriya citti, kuṇa citti, pirakiruticitti, puruṭacitti, vintucitti, paracitti, cuttacitti, kālacitti, kalācitti, vicuvacitti, viyōmacitti, piramacitti, civacitti mutaliya piṇṭacitti, aṇṭacitti, pakiraṇṭa citti, aṇṭāṇṭacitti eṉkiṉṟa antaraṅka pakiraṅka tattuva tattuvi cittikaḷellāvaṟṟaiyum tirukkaṭaik kaṇippāṟ ceyyavallavarāy, caṭānta camaraca cattiyarāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa camaraca cutta caṉmārkka ñāṉikaḷatu citvilācat tiruccapaik kaṇṇē, puṇṇiya vacattāl pukutap peṟṟu maṉaṅkaṉintu vaṇaṅki niṉṟu, 'carva cutantararāya cattiyarkaḷē! iyaṟkai uṇmait taṉipperum patiyāya kaṭavuḷiṉ iyaṟkait tiruvaruṭ camukam irunta vaṇṇam tiruvuḷam paṟṟit tiruvāy malarntu tiruvārttai aḷittaruḷal vēṇṭum' eṉṟu viṇṇappikkiṉṟa tōṟum tiruvārttai aḷittaliṉṟip peruṅkaruṇait tirukkaṇkaḷil āṉantanīr poḻintu cummā irukkiṉṟaṉar eṉṟum, uṇarntōr viyanturaippak kēḷviyuṟṟu, 'iyaṟkait tiruvaruṭ camukam irunta vaṇṇam eṉṉaiyō! eṉṉaiyō!!' eṉṟu kulāvik kulāvik kūvukiṉṟavaṉāṉēṉ.
translation: Those who have realized tell this too. There are the sages of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam. They have full freedom to grant with ease the functions of bringing forth, setting in motion, withdrawing, veiling and making clear all the tattvas and all the tattvis, the beings who preside over the tattvas. They have attained the complete form of the blissful experience of natural true wisdom. They are eternal ones with bodies pure, of sound and of wisdom, which nothing hinders at any time, in any place or in any way. By a gracious glance of their holy eyes they can perform all the attainments, inner and outer, of the tattvas and the tattvis: the attainments of the elements, of the inner faculties, of the senses, of the qualities, of prakriti, of purusha, of bindu, of para, of the pure, of time, of kalā, of the universe, of space, of Brahma, of Siva and the like, which are the attainments of the body; and the attainment of the cosmos, of the outer cosmos and of the cosmos of cosmoses. They shine as the True Ones in whom the six ends are one in harmony. Seekers who, by the power of merit, are granted entry into the holy hall of the play of Consciousness of these sages stand before them with melting hearts, bowing, and petition them: "O True Ones of complete freedom! Be pleased to take it to heart, open your holy lips and grant a holy word on the natural holy presence of Grace of God, the unique great Lord of natural truth, as it is." Yet every time they petition so, the sages give no holy word. Tears of bliss pour from their holy eyes of great compassion, and they remain still. Hearing those who have realized tell this in wonder, I have become one who cries out, rejoicing again and again: "The natural holy presence of Grace as it is: what is it! What is it!!"
commentary: The sentence that began in section 7 ends here, with its frame: Vallalar heard all this from "those who have realized" (uṇarntōr), told in wonder. Their second report concerns the sages of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, who hold the powers listed first. They are wholly free to grant with ease the five functions over all the tattvas and the tattvis; the lords who carry out such functions are bewildered and grieve (sections 2 and 3). They have attained the full form of the blissful experience of natural true wisdom. They are eternal ones with bodies pure, of sound and of wisdom; the words recall the three bodies of the Great True Petition, Suddha Deham, Pranava Deham and Jnana Deham. By a gracious glance they can perform every attainment (citti) of the tattvas and tattvis. They are the True Ones (cattiyar) in whom the six ends of section 7 are one in harmony (camaracam). Seekers granted entry by the power of merit into their holy hall of the play of Consciousness (citvilācam) put the same request to them. Unlike the sages of section 7, who sighed and spoke, these give no word at all. Tears of bliss pour from their eyes of great compassion, and they remain still (cummā irukkiṉṟaṉar). Hearing this, Vallalar cries out, rejoicing again and again: "The natural holy presence of Grace as it is: what is it!"

sections.title: How, Then, Can Your Form Be Known?

tamil: அடிநிலைக் கருமஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், முடிநிலைக் கருமஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், அடிநிலை யோகஞான சித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், முடிநிலை யோகஞான சித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், அடிநிலைத் தத்துவ ஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், முடிநிலைத் தத்துவ ஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், அடிநிலை ஆன்ம ஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், முடிநிலை ஆன்ம ஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், சுத்த ஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், சமரச சுத்த ஞானசித்தி அனுபவங்களினும், அதுஅதுவாகி நிறைந்தும், அதுஅதுவாகி விளங்கியும், அதுஅதுவாகி இனித்தும், ஆங்காங்கு அதீதமாகிக் கலந்தும், இவை அனைத்துமாகி ஒருமித்தும், அதீதாதீதமாகித் தனித்தும் வயங்குகின்ற பெருங் கருணைப் பெரும்பதியாய கடவுளே! எல்லாச் சத்திகளுக்கும், எல்லாச் சத்தர்களுக்கும் எல்லா மூர்த்திகளுக்கும் எல்லா மூர்த்தர்களுக்கும், எல்லாத் தேவிகளுக்கும் எல்லாத் தேவர்களுக்கும் எல்லாச் சாதனர்களுக்கும் எல்லாச் சாத்தியர்களுக்கும் எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் எல்லாத் தத்துவங்களுக்கும் எல்லாப் பொருள்களுக்கும் எல்லாக் குணங்களுக்கும் எல்லாச் செயல்களுக்கும் எல்லா அனுபவங்களுக்கும் மற்றெல்லாவற்றிற்கும் முதற்காரணமாயும் நிமித்த காரணமாயும் துணைக் காரணமாயும் இவை அல்லவாயும் விளங்குகின்ற திருவருட் சமுகம் இருந்த வண்ணம் அறிந்து கொள்ளுதல் இங்ஙனமானால், திருவருட்சமுகப் பெருங்கருணைப் பெரும் பதியாய தேவரீர் இயற்கைத் திருவண்ணம் அறிந்துகொள்ளுதல் எங்ஙனமோ! எங்ஙனமோ!!
translit: aṭinilaik karumañāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, muṭinilaik karumañāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, aṭinilai yōkañāṉa citti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, muṭinilai yōkañāṉa citti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, aṭinilait tattuva ñāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, muṭinilait tattuva ñāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, aṭinilai āṉma ñāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, muṭinilai āṉma ñāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, cutta ñāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, camaraca cutta ñāṉacitti aṉupavaṅkaḷiṉum, atu-atuvāki niṟaintum, atu-atuvāki viḷaṅkiyum, atu-atuvāki iṉittum, āṅkāṅku atītamākik kalantum, ivai aṉaittumāki orumittum, atītātītamākit taṉittum vayaṅkukiṉṟa peruṅ karuṇaip perumpatiyāya kaṭavuḷē! ellāc cattikaḷukkum, ellāc cattarkaḷukkum ellā mūrttikaḷukkum ellā mūrttarkaḷukkum, ellāt tēvikaḷukkum ellāt tēvarkaḷukkum ellāc cātaṉarkaḷukkum ellāc cāttiyarkaḷukkum ellā uyirkaḷukkum ellāt tattuvaṅkaḷukkum ellāp poruḷkaḷukkum ellāk kuṇaṅkaḷukkum ellāc ceyalkaḷukkum ellā aṉupavaṅkaḷukkum maṟṟellāvaṟṟiṟkum mutaṟkāraṇamāyum nimitta kāraṇamāyum tuṇaik kāraṇamāyum ivai allavāyum viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tiruvaruṭ camukam irunta vaṇṇam aṟintu koḷḷutal iṅṅaṉamāṉāl, tiruvaruṭcamukap peruṅkaruṇaip perum patiyāya tēvarīr iyaṟkait tiruvaṇṇam aṟintukoḷḷutal eṅṅaṉamō! eṅṅaṉamō!!
translation: O God, great Lord of great compassion! In the experiences of the attainment of the wisdom of action, at its base stage and at its crowning stage; in the experiences of the attainment of the wisdom of yoga, at its base stage and at its crowning stage; in the experiences of the attainment of the wisdom of the tattvas, at its base stage and at its crowning stage; in the experiences of the attainment of the wisdom of the soul, at its base stage and at its crowning stage; in the experiences of the attainment of pure wisdom; and in the experiences of the attainment of Samarasa pure wisdom: You become each one and fill it, You become each one and shine in it, and You become each one and are sweet in it; in each of them You blend with it as the transcendent; You become all of these and are one; and, as the transcendent beyond the transcendent, You shine alone. The holy presence of Grace shines as the primary cause, the instrumental cause and the supporting cause of all energies and all their agents, all divine forms and all who bear them, all goddesses and all gods, all who practise and all who have attained, all living beings, all tattvas, all things, all qualities, all actions, all experiences and everything else, and it shines also as none of these. If this is how it is with knowing that holy presence of Grace as it is, then how, oh how, can the natural sacred form of You, the great Lord of great compassion of the holy presence of Grace, be known!
commentary: In the Tamil, the call to God and the question after it are one sentence. Vallalar first names God by what He is in every experience of attainment (citti), in his own order. Four kinds come first, each at its base stage and at its crowning stage: the attainment of the wisdom of action (karuma ñāṉam), of yoga, of the tattvas and of the soul (āṉma ñāṉam). Then come pure wisdom (cutta ñāṉam) and, last, Samarasa pure wisdom (camaraca cutta ñāṉam). In every one of these experiences God becomes that very experience: He fills it, shines in it and is its sweetness. In each He is also the transcendent (atītam), blended with it. He becomes all of them and is one, and He shines alone as the transcendent beyond the transcendent (atītātītam). Then comes the conclusion. The holy presence of Grace is the cause of everything in three ways. For a pot, the primary cause is the clay it is made of, the instrumental cause is the potter who makes it, and the supporting cause is his wheel and stick. The holy presence of Grace is all three for all energies and their agents, all divine forms and those who bear them, all goddesses and gods, all who practise and all who have attained, all living beings, all tattvas, things, qualities, actions and experiences, and everything else; and it is also none of these. The sages could not tell even this holy presence as it is: some sighed, and others wept tears of bliss and remained still. How then could anyone know the natural sacred form of God Himself, the great Lord of great compassion of that holy presence?

sections.title: Knowing without Knowing

tamil: ஓ! ஒப்புயர்வின்றி விளங்குகின்ற ஒருவரே! தேவரீர் திருவண்ணமும் திருவருட் சமுகத் திருவண்ணமும் அறிதற்கும் கருதுதற்கும் துதித்தற்கும் எத்திறத்தானும் கூடாவாயினும் அடிமை அளவிற்கு இயன்றபடி அறியாது அறிந்தும் கருதாது கருதியும் துதியாது துதித்தும் எனது உரிமையை ஊற்றஞ் செய்கின்றவனானேன். வந்தனம்! வந்தனம்!!
திருச்சிற்றம்பலம்
translit: ō! oppuyarviṉṟi viḷaṅkukiṉṟa oruvarē! tēvarīr tiruvaṇṇamum tiruvaruṭ camukat tiruvaṇṇamum aṟitaṟkum karututaṟkum tutittaṟkum ettiṟattāṉum kūṭāvāyiṉum aṭimai aḷaviṟku iyaṉṟapaṭi aṟiyātu aṟintum karutātu karutiyum tutiyātu tutittum eṉatu urimaiyai ūṟṟañ ceykiṉṟavaṉāṉēṉ. vantaṉam! vantaṉam!!
tirucciṟṟampalam
translation: O You, the One who shines with none equal and none above! Your own sacred form, and the sacred form of the holy presence of Grace, cannot be known, contemplated or praised in any way at all. Even so, as far as a servant is able, knowing without knowing, contemplating without contemplating and praising without praising, I have made firm my right. Salutations! Salutations!! Tiruchitrambalam.
commentary: Vallalar calls on God as the One who shines with none equal and none above. All that he has heard leads here: neither God's own sacred form nor the sacred form of the holy presence of Grace can be known, contemplated or praised in any way at all. He had longed to know the natural truth of the holy presence of Grace, to contemplate its great compassion and to praise its great glory, and he began, holding to the word of the sages of true wisdom that God has every form that knowers know, contemplators contemplate and praisers praise (section 5). Now, as far as a servant (aṭimai) can, he has known without knowing, contemplated without contemplating and praised without praising, and so he has made firm his right (urimai). The three words that run through the whole petition, know, contemplate and praise, come back here for the last time. The petition closes with a twofold salutation, vantaṉam, and, as it began, with Tiruchitrambalam.

works.title: The True Petition of the Sangam of the Universal Pure True Path
